<a id="observation"></a>
### Observation

Partial · coverage 92% · macOS 14.0 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/observation) · REA `ev_59ddd532abf1677b1e3304c8d7443c1ffaef9a4e65513f0e7e8dd952321415d0`

BifrOSt has manual value observation: an Observable<T> that notifies subscribers only when the value changes, with Combine-style sink, map and remove_duplicates. A set made inside a subscriber is queued and delivered in order, and cancelling a subscriber during a change sticks. with_observation_tracking records the observables a closure reads and fires one on-change callback; Observable::observations pulls changes in order. A declarative observable_model! macro gives a model struct with one change publisher, so a property write notifies the owner. It still has no derive, no tracking options or tokens, no continuous observation, and no async sequence.

| Feature | Apple API | BifrOSt | Status | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Observable conformance (@Observable macro) | Observable() macro, Observable protocol | springboard/sdk/src/observable_object.rs (observable_model! macro) | Partial | Declarative macro: observable_model! { struct Name { field: T = init } } gives a struct whose fields are Observable<T>, all linked to one ObservableObject publisher. No derive, so no per-property opt-out (ObservationIgnored) and no computed properties. No app uses the macro yet (only its tests). Built on parity/team-a-09; not yet verified on Midget. |
| Change notification on value change | Observable protocol, ObservationRegistrar | springboard/sdk/src/observable.rs (Observable::set, update, subscribe, sink); springboard/ui/src/observe.rs (Observable<T>::set, subscribe(old, new)) | Parity | verified on Midget 0.7.25 by 23 tests. Notifies only when the value differs (PartialEq) in the UI-model copy; the SDK copy notifies on every set. A set made from inside a subscriber is queued and delivered after the running change, in order (fixed in SDK, was dropped). Cancelling another subscriber during a change is now durable. UI-model copy (ui/src/observe.rs) is unchanged: its subscribers receive old and new values only. |
| Automatic dependency tracking | withObservationTracking(_:onChange:), withObservationTracking(options:_:onChange:) | springboard/sdk/src/observable.rs (with_observation_tracking, Observable::get records reads) | Parity | verified on Midget 0.7.25 by 23 tests. with_observation_tracking(apply, on_change) records each Observable read by get() inside apply and calls on_change once when one changes; the tracking then ends. Apple's withObservationTracking returns only the closure value and also covers options, and its onChange runs before the change; here on_change runs after the change, and reads inside on_change are not tracked. Only the SDK Observable is tracked; the UI-model copy is not. |
| Async change sequence | Observations, withContinuousObservation(options:apply:) | springboard/sdk/src/observable.rs (Observable::observations, Observations::try_next, pending_len) | Parity | verified on Midget 0.7.25 by 23 tests. Pull-based sequence of the changes after the call, oldest first; dropping it stops recording. It is the synchronous counterpart of Apple's Observations: it has no suspension, no AsyncSequence conformance and no withContinuousObservation(options:apply:). |
| Observation tracking options and tokens | ObservationTracking, ObservationTracking.Options, ObservationTracking.Token, ObservationTracking.Event | springboard/sdk/src/observable.rs (Subscription, Cancellables) | Parity | verified on Midget 0.7.25 by 23 tests. Subscription cancels on drop (AnyCancellable). No event or options types for tracking. |
| Ignore or track individual properties | ObservationIgnored(), ObservationTracked() | n/a | n/a | Macro-only behaviour of the Swift language; with no macro in BifrOSt there is nothing to mark. |
| Notifications from system state | Observation Registrar for model state (manual) | springboard/sdk/src/process_info.rs (observe_thermal_state, observe_low_power_mode); docs/bifrost-ui.md:1214 (NotificationCenter add_observer, post); docs/bifrost-ui.md:1542 (workspace observe) | Parity | verified on Midget 0.7.25 by 4 tests. Observer-style subscriptions exist for system events (NotificationCenter, workspace, thermal state, Low Power Mode). They are not Observation's property-level tracking. |

Gaps: No derive for the @Observable macro: model properties are listed in observable_model!, and there is no per-property opt-out. with_observation_tracking tracks only SDK Observable reads.; No withContinuousObservation(options:apply:), ObservationTracking.Options, Event or Token: with_observation_tracking is one-shot and returns only the closure value.; Observations is pull-based (try_next), not an AsyncSequence; there is no executor or suspension in the pure std model.; docs/bifrost-ui.md:1435 still describes the old re-entrant set limit; that shared doc is out of scope for this change and is listed for a later update.; SwiftUI-style integration (view invalidation from observed model state) not verified in code; no binding found in this pass..

<a id="statereporting"></a>
### StateReporting

Partial · coverage 83% · macOS 27.0 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/statereporting) · REA `ev_4cfeac83cd2c0731855ab3128406c1847326babab9f3f5b2823e289fbcb188b3`

StateReporting lets an app define named domains, report one active state per domain and attach reportable metadata, so that MetricKit and Instruments can attribute crashes and metrics to app state. BifrOSt has no app-facing state-transition or metadata API. Its system layer captures crash.log entries, offers a Share with Developer action and unified logging; these cover the diagnostics side but not the state attribution.

### SwiftData

Partial · coverage 88% · macOS 14.0 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/swiftdata) · REA `ev_563b0360c56d3e1d3ca6e344e289dcc2215e1be7433634f4f0175d1860ff401e`

SwiftData is a declarative object-graph layer over a store: @Model classes, ModelContainer and ModelContext, predicate queries, relationships, undo, history and iCloud sync. BifrOSt has no model layer or database-backed store and no SDK API for one; apps persist with flat files, a key-value defaults file, JSON restoration state and an in-memory undo manager, which cover some pieces of the same job but not the model, query or sync parts.

Partial · coverage 81% · macOS 10.15 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/swiftui) · REA `ev_bbfb997837e04677c361c8a1baef569207c04cd765d58ab1f277e3f1865f456a`

Imperative equivalents exist for gestures, shortcuts, focus, clipboard, drag and drop, and an AT-SPI accessibility bridge. Custom rotors and the display accommodation flags (reduce motion, increase contrast) now exist for apps (sdk/src/accessibility_rotor.rs, sdk/src/accessibility_display.rs). There is no declarative modifier API, no app-facing announcement call, and no Xcode tooling.

### SwiftUI (Views, View layout)

Partial · coverage 62% · macOS 10.15 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/swiftui) · REA `ev_1a882830e38c95f440f0bd336bd00c74fb8bc2a84fc97d1342e354040edb662e`

BifrOSt has an imperative, retained-view toolkit with stacks, grids, forms, scroll views, source lists, tables and animation, plus Auto Layout style constraints. It has no declarative View protocol, modifier chain, state-driven body, shapes or custom Layout protocol.

<a id="symbols"></a>
### Symbols

Partial · coverage 70% · macOS 14.0 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/symbols) · REA `ev_4228c223ea1ec28dfa7061baa7d6168c30cb9d1b86003c9d7dcf0cab875728f3`

The Symbols framework is Apple's set of universal symbol effects (appear, bounce, pulse, variableColor, replace and others) for SF Symbols images in AppKit, UIKit and SwiftUI. BifrOSt has a fixed set of 59 hand-drawn line glyphs named after SF Symbols and a generic implicit animation system, but no symbol-effect API and no symbol layers or rendering modes, so none of the effects can be applied to a symbol image.

Not the SF Symbols catalogue. The 22-symbol set maps names and code points (springboard/render/tests/parity_sdk-tests-10-w7.rs). The renderer's symbol font path finds no real symbol font on the device, so the drawings are what ships |
| Symbol drawing: shape painters and named icons | No direct counterpart; the fill behind a symbol image (CGContext fill of a path into a rect) | springboard/sdk/src/glyph_draw.rs (paint, disc, ring, segment, arc, ellipse, either, globe, mic, dismiss_keyboard, alarm_clock, stopwatch, timer re-exported from springboard/render/src/sdf_glyphs.rs; springboard/src/shell/glyphs.rs re-exports the same); springboard/sdk/src/symbol_draw.rs (SymbolStyle, paint_layer) | Partial | The shell's painters are the SDK's, and bifrost_app::symbol_draw applies a symbol's weight stroke factor, scale, rendering mode (hierarchical opacity by layer, palette slots, monochrome) and palette to each layer (headless tests in sdk/tests/parity_sdk-complete-34.rs). Gap: the named icons (globe, mic and the others) still take one colour per call with no layered form, and a Midget check is still needed for parity. |

Wave 2 (symbols, parity/integration e52c2fd0): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. no SDK type or call applies a symbol effect to a glyph; glyphs are drawn once per frame with no per-layer state |

<a id="usdkit"></a>
### USDKit (App Frameworks)

n/a · coverage n/a · macOS 27.0 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/usdkit) · REA `ev_d51a6d19c6b73d95ec87738a62923a1efff6ea4ab3642e71fabb161b525697e8`

USDKit authors and renders 3D Universal Scene Description stages through RealityKit. BifrOSt has no USD reader or writer, no 3D scene graph and no 3D rendering API for apps, and the framework depends on Apple's RealityKit stack, so there is no sensible BifrOSt counterpart.

| Feature | Apple API | BifrOSt | Status | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Stages, prims and layers (USD composition) | USDStage, USDPrim, USDLayer | nothing found | n/a | Apple doc: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/usdkit (Essentials). BifrOSt has no USD document model. |
| Values and tokens | USDValue, USDValueProtocol, USDToken | nothing found | n/a | Apple doc: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/usdkit (Values and tokens). |
| Transforms | USDTransformOperation | nothing found | n/a | Apple doc: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/usdkit (Transforms). Transforms in the SDK are 2D view transforms only. |
| RealityKit rendering of a stage | USDStageComponent | nothing found | n/a | Depends on RealityKit, an Apple-only rendering stack. Apple doc: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/usdkit (RealityKit rendering and playback). |
| Timeline playback of a stage | USDPlayer | nothing found | n/a | Apple doc: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/usdkit (RealityKit rendering and playback). |
| Render diagnostics | USDRenderError | nothing found | n/a | Apple doc: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/usdkit (Render diagnostics). |

<a id="visual-intelligence"></a>
### Visual Intelligence

Partial · coverage 83% · macOS 27.0 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/visualintelligence) · REA `ev_7363bdc6dc7795ace62ea12ce957cc5ae911ee04ad4b7676496c893b9e2726f7`

Apple's framework is an app-side search hook: the system passes a captured camera or screenshot scene to an app, which returns matching content through App Intents. BifrOSt has no visual search and no scene-to-app delivery. Its App Intents, entity query and Core Spotlight code cover the App Intents half, which is only partly the same contract; the Apple Intelligence classification and Siri schemas have no counterpart.

| Feature | Apple API | BifrOSt | Status | Note |

Apple's Accounts framework is deprecated (landing page: for new apps, use the service provider's SDK). BifrOSt has no system account store, no account types, no OAuth credential objects and no access-grant prompt for third-party accounts. The closest pieces are a per-app keychain for opaque secrets and the local OS account used for desktop sign-in.

<a id="application-services"></a>
### Application Services

Partial · coverage 75% · macOS 10.0 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/applicationservices) · REA `ev_aa67df2e51e2916455b18b5705ec62cb03dcae34a55905e84b9fc3290a9c1ff9`

Application Services is mostly legacy Carbon C API (Apple Event Manager, ColorSync, Speech Synthesis, PDEPlugIn, HIShape, Translation). BifrOSt covers the pasteboard, the accessibility tree (AT-SPI2 instead of AXUIElement), and printing through CUPS; colour profile conversion exists in the render crate (springboard/render/src/cg/color.rs) but not as an app API; speech synthesis and the print-plug-in and shape APIs have no counterpart.

<a id="automaticassessmentconfiguration"></a>
### Automatic Assessment Configuration

n/a · coverage n/a · macOS 10.15.4 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/automaticassessmentconfiguration) · REA `ev_eaa0e9e64b37e4052ad5e89b7bafd5395050072da18dfff1788cb8c593dc676d`

Automatic Assessment Configuration starts a locked exam session, limiting desktop features. It needs an Apple-issued entitlement granted to educational apps on Apple's platforms. BifrOSt has no assessment or exam lockdown mode, and the feature is tied to Apple's entitlement process.

| Assessment errors | AEAssessmentError, AEAssessmentErrorDomain | nothing found | n/a | Errors from the session above |
| Allowed binaries | AEAssessmentBinaryExecutable, AEAssessmentBinaryExecutableConfiguration | springboard/src/bare/app_policy.rs (bubblewrap sandbox) | n/a | The sandbox isolates apps but is not an exam lockdown; no exam allow-list API |
| Menu bar items kept during assessment | AEMenuBarItem, AEAppleMenuItem | springboard/src/shell/desktop_bar.rs (menu bar) | n/a | The menu bar has no assessment mode; the framework's structures have no counterpart |
| Account type for session | AEUserAccountType | nothing found | n/a | Apple account types; no exam account role |

BifrOSt has a shell-internal local contact store (one flat file, fixed fields, atomic save) that the Contacts app, Search and Share use directly. Apps read and save contacts through the SDK contacts module and the contacts service, behind a per-app access grant. Groups (nested) and a polled change history exist; containers do not. Apps with a contacts read grant get system.contacts.change when the store file changes.

<a id="contacts-ui"></a>
### Contacts UI

Partial · coverage 67% · macOS 10.11 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/contactsui) · REA `ev_6fb05553c10a345f6320e9c365f241ee7902da18913291c6e693fb6100143bc4`

Apple's Contacts UI is three view controllers or controls: a contact viewer, a contact picker, and a limited-access button. BifrOSt has no SDK viewer or editor view, and no SDK picker that returns a chosen contact to an app. Apps reach the contact store through the SDK contacts module behind a per-app access grant, and the Contacts app's picker model drives its Add People flow. The card and editor stay private to the Contacts app.

Wired into the UI in wiring wave 3 (0.5.39); verify on Midget for parity. |

Saving happens when the form is done, and Cancel leaves the contact unchanged. Not exposed as an SDK API. |

<a id="core-ai"></a>
### Core AI

Partial · coverage 80% · macOS 27.0 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/coreai) · REA `ev_d5a497b99b8bee740ff9134aa7978e7596ef3614efb76bbb2ec57ef802f765e0`

Core AI runs specialized models on Apple silicon (CPU, GPU, Neural Engine) with model assets, cached specialization, inference functions and tensor types. BifrOSt runs small dense, relu and softmax models on the CPU through bifrost_app::core_ai (typed inference functions, cached plans); it has no GPU or large-model runtime and no compute stream that runs work. Its AI features call the Anthropic cloud API, and its predictive text is a trie with bigrams.

### Core Data

Partial · coverage 93% · macOS 10.4 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/coredata) · REA `ev_8c61ec290207e2cd99f86f147191b4795ea108ce4a651c63d4fc56d57c43168a`

BifrOSt has no object graph, managed object context, fetch request or persistent store layer. Apps persist their data as small atomically replaced text or JSON files through Codable, UserDefaults and the document layer, and the undo manager and snapshot diffing cover some of what Core Data's undo and table data sources do. Persistent history, migrations and CloudKit mirroring have no on-device counterpart; sync exists only as server-side counters in bifrost-cloud.

Wave 6 (b03, main): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on Midget. No managed store abstraction; each app writes its own files in its data directory. No SQLite-backed store. |
| Data modeling (object graph and relationships) | Core Data model editor, NSManagedObjectModel, NSEntityDescription, NSRelationshipDescription (https://developer.apple.com/documentation/coredata/modeling-data) | springboard/sdk/src/object_graph.rs (Model, Entity, Relationship) | Parity | verified on Midget 0.7.25 by 10 tests. Wave 6 (b03, main): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on Midget. Codable encodes a value tree per type by hand or with the codable! macro. There is no entity model, no relationships and no inverse tracking. |
| Managed objects and contexts | NSManagedObject, NSManagedObjectContext (https://developer.apple.com/documentation/coredata/nsmanagedobjectcontext) | springboard/sdk/src/object_graph.rs (Context) | Parity | verified on Midget 0.7.25 by 10 tests. Wave 6 (b03, main): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on Midget. Apps keep plain Rust structs in memory and rewrite the whole store on save. No faulting, no per-object dirty tracking, no context isolation. |

Gap: faults are held in the same process, so there is no database store beneath them.; No database-backed store, so stores are rewritten whole on each save and do not scale past the bounded lists (contacts MAX_ITEMS 10000, calendar MAX_EVENTS 2048).; No persistent history or transaction log of store changes.; No migration path between store versions (lightweight, staged or manual).; No fetched results controller that binds a query to a table or list.; No on-device CloudKit-style mirroring or sharing; sync exists only as server-side counters in bifrost-cloud..

Related: [SwiftData](#swiftdata), [Foundation (Files and Data Persistence)](#foundation-files-persistence), [AppKit (App Structure)](#appkit-app-structure), [Core Services](#core-services), [Swift](#swift).

Apple's framework gives apps device position, heading, geofences, beacons and geocoding behind a permission prompt. BifrOSt has an SDK location module (LocationManager, reverse and forward geocoding) that the shell answers from a fixed location set in Settings, with a location permission sheet; there is no device position source, no location manifest permission, and no geofence or heading feed for apps.

Core Motion reports accelerometer, gyroscope, magnetometer, pedometer, altitude and activity data from device sensors. BifrOSt has a shared model for raw accelerometer and gyroscope updates and for device motion (attitude, gravity, rotation rate), exposed to apps through the SDK. The shell's sensor feed now drives screen orientation from device motion (built 2026-10-17, not yet checked on hardware). The magnetometer, altitude, activity and pedometer readers are not built; their models are re-exported by the SDK only.

The attitude frame is arbitrary (no magnetometer). The shell does not read it yet. <a id="core-spotlight"></a>
### Core Spotlight

Partial · coverage 65% · macOS 10.13 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/corespotlight) · REA `ev_4438bf59535e4bd6ba0ca70598c6a17e34d2cbccb6b6a1ca563a4e22a50cb41b`

BifrOSt covers the core indexing path: an app can add, replace and delete its own searchable items, the shell keeps a bounded per-app index, and the system Search panel lists the items under Documents, ordered by a hybrid ranker (BM25 over title and text, title match, indexing recency, local open counts; the semantic term is a hook with no local model yet). The Search panel queries its sources (apps, Settings, clock, Deildu, contacts, shortcuts, files, calendar) concurrently with a deadline and streams late sections in. A query, suggestion and assistant search tool exist as host-tested models over the same matching. CSSearchQuery reaches the shell's search-index service; the delegate and tool models are not wired yet, index extension requests are a model, and the Foundation pipeline types are not built.

| Feature | Apple API | BifrOSt | Status | Note |

Dates, authors, type and searchable custom values are folded into the indexed keywords. Host tests only; verify on Midget for parity. Gaps: Streamed found-items replies are not built: CSSearchQuery gets all hits at once. The query language (ui quicksearch_query.rs) has attribute comparisons, wildcards, && and \|\|.; The shell does not pull from an index extension on protection-class or throttling events; it asks once per run when an app has no items. CSImportExtension is not built.; The default index is one JSON file per app, sealed with the shell's key (spotindex.rs), with oldest-first eviction at 1000 items; the named-index descriptions carry only the name and protection class.; The Foundation models search tool is a model only: SpotlightSearchTool is not offered to the assistant app, and the pipeline types (SearchSource, CustomStage, SearchResultsTable and the rest) are not modelled..

BifrOSt has a TrueType and CFF font engine with metrics, cmap glyph lookup, variable-font axes and an attributed string model with line wrapping and truncation. It has no app-facing font objects, font manager, OpenType shaping (kerning, ligatures outside colour emoji), paragraph styles, tabs, bidi or vertical text.

<a id="crashreportextension"></a>
### CrashReportExtension

OS only · coverage 64% · macOS 27.0 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/crashreportextension) · REA `ev_e3418b95610b968252223751baf4860e5de668b1c88d59df6389a9f3e42a89a3`

Apple's framework is an out-of-process app extension that lets a developer inspect a crashed app (reason, binary images, symbolication, a read-only corpse port) and send its own report. BifrOSt captures crashes at the system level only: the shell's panic hook and the Linux coredump list. No app-facing SDK API inspects another crashed process or builds a report from it.

| Feature | Apple API | BifrOSt | Status | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Crash reporter extension point (CrashReporterExtension, processCrashReport(process:)) | CrashReporterExtension protocol, processCrashReport(process:), com.apple.crash-reporter.extension extension point | springboard/sdk/src/crash_report.rs | Parity | verified on Midget 0.7.25 by 9 tests. Wave 3 (theme-14, parity/integration cf8e852d): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. No app extension mechanism lets an app's own code run when another app crashes. Apple's handler runs out of process; BifrOSt has no equivalent hook. |
| Crash reason (CrashedProcess.reason, CrashReason) | CrashedProcess.reason, CrashReason | springboard/sdk/src/crash_report.rs (CrashReason, ProcessCrash::reason); springboard/src/shell/diag.rs (CrashEntry signature, from crash.log); springboard/apps/console-desktop/src/model.rs (parse_coredump_list: SIG mapped to Fault) | Partial | The SDK's ProcessCrash carries the reason text and CrashReason displays it, tested headless in springboard/sdk/tests/parity_sdk-os-03.rs. Gap: the shell does not pass a crashed app's reason to an app's reporter, so the reason reaches an app only when the caller builds the record. |
| Binary images and symbolication (binaryImages, symbolicateAddress(es), SymbolicatedFrame) | CrashedProcess.binaryImages, BinaryImageInfo, symbolicateAddress(_:), symbolicateAddresses(_:), symbolAddress(imageName:symbolName:) | springboard/sdk/src/crash_report.rs | Parity | verified on Midget 0.7.25 by 9 tests. Wave 3 (theme-14, parity/integration cf8e852d): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. Symbolication is done by hand (coredumpctl and gdb, per the diagnose-crash skill). No SDK call maps addresses to symbols inside another process. |
| Corpse port (corpsePort, read-only Mach port) | CrashedProcess.corpsePort | none | n/a | Mach ports are an Apple kernel mechanism. The Linux equivalent is the core file, which is not exposed to apps. |
| Sending a report to the developer | Extension sends its report to the developer's own server after collection | springboard/src/shell/diag.rs (bundle shared with the developer, parse_log, upload_url, post); springboard/src/shell/diagnostics_page.rs (Diagnostics page) | Partial | The crash log parsing, the bundle layout and its HTTPS-only upload rule are tested headless in springboard/tests/parity_sdk-tests-01.rs. Gap: the bundle covers the shell only, and no app can send its own crash report through an SDK API. |
| Crash record written by the shell and the runtime | Framework-level crash data, collected by the system on crash | springboard/sdk/src/crash_record.rs (parse_entry, parse_log, parse_panic, parse_last_exit, ended_uncleanly); springboard/src/bare/crashlog.rs (writer: crash.log, last_exit, last_start, unclean-run note); springboard/mcp/src/dev.rs (panic_log) | Partial | Typed readers for crash.log entries, panic locations, the last_exit marker and the unclean-run check are tested headless in springboard/sdk/tests/parity_sdk-rest-07.rs. Gap: the shell's writer does not use these readers, and no app is granted its own records. |
| Crashed web content process notice | WebKit process-termination callback (closest counterpart in the Web content API, not in CrashReportExtension) | springboard/sdk/src/webview.rs ("crashed" event, line 732); docs/bifrost-ui.md section "WebProcessPool crash recovery" | Partial | Web engine crashes reach the app as an event, and the browser restarts the engine. This is the closest SDK surface, but it covers web content only and does not produce a crash report. |
| Crash log presentation in the Console app | Not part of the framework (Console and Xcode Organizer read crash reports) | springboard/apps/console-desktop/src/source.rs (coredump source); springboard/apps/console-desktop/src/model.rs (parse_coredump_list test) | OS only | A system app reads the coredump list. No SDK API exposes it to third-party apps: a core dump holds another app's memory image, and no sandbox grant lets an app read one yet. |

Gaps: No app extension point for an app to run its own crash handler on another app's crash (the CrashReporterExtension role).; The SDK crash report model takes a crashed process's reason and binary images as values and symbolicates addresses (sdk crash_report.rs); no shell path feeds it yet.; No SDK API for an app to build and send a crash report to its own server; the only path is the manual diagnostics bundle.; Crash records for apps come from systemd-coredump; the SDK does not surface them to apps..

Create ML trains Core ML models (image, video, text, sound, motion and tabular) on the Mac, using Apple's ML toolchain and playgrounds. BifrOSt has no model training tool and no Core ML equivalent, and a desktop shell has no sensible counterpart for an Apple-only training pipeline.

| Feature | Apple API | BifrOSt | Status | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Image models | MLImageClassifier, MLObjectDetector, MLHandPoseClassifier | none | n/a | image classifier training is tied to the Core ML toolchain |
| Video models | MLActionClassifier, MLHandActionClassifier, MLStyleTransfer | none | n/a | no video model training |
| Text models | MLTextClassifier, MLWordTagger, MLGazetteer, MLWordEmbedding | none | n/a | the keyboard word predictor (springboard/apps/keyboard/src/predict.rs) is a word list, not a trained model |
| Sound and motion models | MLSoundClassifier, MLActivityClassifier | none | n/a | no audio or motion model training |
| Tabular models and data | MLClassifier, MLRegressor, MLRecommender, MLDataTable | none | n/a | no tabular training API; the SDK has no data-table model |
| Model accuracy and metrics | MLClassifierMetrics, MLRegressorMetrics, MLObjectDetectorMetrics | none | n/a | no evaluation metrics for trained models |
| Training control | MLJob, MLTrainingSession, MLTrainingSessionParameters, MLCheckpoint | none | n/a | no asynchronous training sessions |

Gaps: No model training tool or training session API of any kind (none in springboard/sdk/src/ or springboard/ui/src/).; The SDK runs small text-form models of dense, relu and softmax layers (sdk core_ml.rs); no other model formats and no training..

| Attestation object validation | Attestation Object Validation Guide (server side) | none | n/a | Server verifies Apple-signed objects; not applicable to BifrOSt |
| Server-to-server fraud risk data | Assessing fraud risk (server-to-server calls) | none | n/a | Apple service only |
| Error reporting | DCError, DCErrorDomain | none | n/a | Only meaningful with DeviceCheck itself |

Gaps: Nothing to match: the service is Apple-hardware and Apple-server bound (App Attest needs Apple's attestation service and device keys).

<a id="javascriptcore"></a>
### JavaScriptCore

Partial · coverage 57% · macOS 10.5 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/javascriptcore) · REA `ev_fa2c7a0f3a85b1b57f903a371c17c1126d97616db84c50315f50f10e76b9ad58`

JavaScriptCore lets an app run JavaScript on its own, exchange values with it, and expose its objects to scripts. BifrOSt now has the JsContext equivalent (bifrost_app::js_context: a standalone Boa realm, typed values, host functions, exceptions, console capture) and still runs scripts inside a web view through evaluateJavaScript. Missing: a shared virtual machine, managed values, exporting Rust types as classes, timers, and the C API.

| Feature | Apple API | BifrOSt | Status | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Execution environment (virtual machine and context) | JSVirtualMachine, JSContext | springboard/sdk/src/js_value.rs (JsValue::from_eval, JsValue::to_literal); springboard/sdk/src/script_value.rs (ScriptValue); springboard/src/shell/browser/js/mod.rs (one Boa Context per browser tab, internal to the Browser); springboard/src/shell/js_context.rs (JsContext); springboard/sdk/src/js_context.rs (bifrost_app::js_context) | Partial | 2026-10-19: apps get a standalone context. JsContext is a fresh Boa realm with no DOM, network, timers or file access, evaluate_script at global scope (var and function definitions persist between calls), loop, recursion and stack limits that turn a runaway script into an exception, console capture with levels, and a source size cap. Still missing: JSVirtualMachine sharing between contexts, JSManagedValue, garbage collector hooks, import, timers. <a id="media-intents"></a>
### Media Intents

Partial · coverage 81% · macOS 27.0 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/mediaintents) · REA `ev_a39e06deb47221d7e378a755d1f9e231b874c4f5a1b7589e72ffdd0e9beeafe4`

Media Intents is the Siri audio search and playback type set (AudioSearch) that Apple delivers through App Intents. BifrOSt has the App Intents side (typed intents and entity queries, no Siri or voice), a per-app audio playback service with shell now-playing controls, and a pure model of the search request, its criteria and catalogue matching (springboard/ui/src/media_search.rs). Nothing routes requests from the system to apps, and there is no voice path.

<a id="multipeer-connectivity"></a>
### Multipeer Connectivity

OS only · coverage 73% · macOS 10.10 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/multipeerconnectivity) · REA `ev_b3b5c0bde001c7ec68d2f53dd69e9886ae8810ea152c2af72aa30cb096c10c5f`

BifrOSt has nearby LAN discovery and one-shot file and byte transfer between devices, run by the shell (UDP beacon on 224.0.0.251:5354, TCP transfer with an explicit Accept). Apps get no SDK API for peers, sessions, invitations or messages, and nothing is encrypted in transit; the MultipeerConnectivity session model is not covered.

Gap: there is no found or lost peer delegate, and the shell's beacon does not yet browse an app's service type. |

BifrOSt has a word tokenizer (alphanumeric runs for spelling) and pattern-based data detection for links, dates, addresses and phone numbers. Partial · coverage 80% · macOS 10.1 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/preferencepanes) · REA `ev_db4bcaa92796c2404b766868425e19d408c6e791746e5b1425684b78be6c2b58`

Apple's framework lets third-party bundles plug panes into System Settings, with a lifecycle (select, unselect veto) and Help menu keys. The SDK has a Quick Look panel model (items, clamped index, Space toggle, arrow stepping), a multi-page PDF layout with page thumbnails beside the content, and a thumbnail path and cache, and the shell draws the floating panel (resizable, full-screen, PDF pages, font samples, audio and video transport). <a id="safari-services"></a>
### Safari Services

Partial · coverage 77% · macOS 10.12 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/safariservices) · REA `ev_db48755bdd049ac960cdd61e81535120a7dc9a2c45e56e809f496825a5b51dc8`

BifrOSt has a WebKit-style web view for SDK apps (WebProcessPool over the Servo engine) and a full Browser app with tabs, history, bookmarks, reader mode and private windows. It has a shared-login session model that no shell code drives yet, but no Safari extension, content blocker, Reading List, universal link, or standard in-app Safari sheet API.

No hover, drag selection, context menus, select/file panels, or cancel of a load (Servo 0.7.0 limits). |

<a id="sms-and-call-reporting"></a>
### SMS and Call Reporting (IdentityLookup)

n/a · coverage n/a · macOS 10.15 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/identitylookup) · REA `ev_8db478d9e08e0d597ac2418892390a98d36e2501b5e3c0deb8d7ddf22622e844`

IdentityLookup is app extensions for SMS/MMS filtering, spam reporting and Live Caller ID Lookup, all tied to the cellular phone and Apple's call directory. BifrOSt has no telephony, SMS or call-blocking stack, so there is no counterpart.

| Feature | Apple API | BifrOSt | Status | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SMS and MMS message filtering | Message Filter app extension (SMS and MMS Message Filtering) | nothing found | n/a | no SMS or MMS stack on BifrOSt PC |
| Spam reporting | Unwanted Communication app extension (SMS and Call Spam Reporting) | nothing found | n/a | no phone calls or SMS to report |
| Live Caller ID Lookup | LiveCallerIDLookupManager, LiveCallerIDLookupProtocol, CallLookupExtensionStatus | nothing found | n/a | requires the system call directory; no telephony on the PC |
| Call blocking and identity data payloads (PIR) | Formatting data for blocking and identity information; HTTP endpoints for Live Caller ID Lookup | nothing found | n/a | server-side protocol tied to the Apple call directory |


Related: [Core Telephony](#core-telephony), [Device Management](#device-management), [IdentityDocumentServices](#identitydocumentservices), [PushKit](#pushkit), [Group Activities](#group-activities).

<a id="social"></a>
### Social

Partial · coverage 67% · macOS 10.8 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/social) · REA `ev_d8070e35a0b4a4bf77a71cd477acdf308f271f04addcec3639691b3fb911a8f3`

Apple's Social framework composes a post to a social network and signs HTTP requests with the user's social account. BifrOSt has a share sheet that passes text, URLs and files to installed apps, a generic HTTP client, a service request model with multipart bodies, a draft that becomes a POST, and an account store with OAuth 1.0a and bearer signing. Nothing signs in an account or posts to a network yet.

### Speech

Partial · coverage 78% · macOS 10.15 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/speech) · REA `ev_83d419f1903e2491c4d2f87ecace3e8a120a051be00d72c9640c0513b97e4722`

The Speech framework does speech-to-text on live or recorded audio. BifrOSt has no recognizer, no transcription module and no SDK API for it. The audio service can record microphone audio to WAV on explicit user request, which a recognizer could later consume. The keyboard's dictation key is a glyph that does nothing when tapped.

Pure model with host unit tests (speech_recognizer.rs, recognition.rs); not wired into the shell or apps, not tested on Midget. No transcription anywhere in springboard/sdk/src or springboard/ui/src. Apple's SpeechAnalyzer and module classes have no counterpart. Built 2026-10-17: on-device recognition through the gst-plugin-whisper element: the pipeline argv and transcript parser (bifrost_ui::whisper; tests whisper::tests), the shell service speech_recognizer (shell::services::recognizer::tests) and the SDK client and backend (bifrost_app speech_whisper::tests). TipKit is a contextual-tip framework: tip content, display rules, a persistent datastore, inline and popover views, and test hooks. <a id="user-notifications"></a>
### User Notifications

Partial · coverage 70% · macOS 10.14 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/usernotifications) · REA `ev_153a89a120dc24e492871ed0c620f9e424d1d5c3b695af681112f5e45a5487f4`

Local notifications are covered: categories with buttons, destructive and text-reply actions, requests with title, subtitle, body, thread, category, a time-interval delay and a Dock badge, removal and listing of delivered and pending requests, and the user's response (also queued for an app that is not running). Remote push (APNs, device tokens, background push) and location triggers are not covered. Calendar and interval triggers, attachments, per-request sounds, the authorization and settings queries and the foreground presentation delegate exist; the notification service extension and communication notifications are models that the shell does not run yet.

### User Notifications UI

Partial · coverage 62% · macOS 11.0 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/usernotificationsui) · REA `ev_e426325cd580d278abf41dd9987944c7903fc63dfcd70d6880f16fa8db867358`

Apple's framework is one extension point: a notification content app extension (UNNotificationContentExtension) that supplies the view for a notification, with custom action handling and media play/pause controls. BifrOSt has no app-supplied notification view; its shell draws banner, lock-screen and Notification Center cards itself, and apps get delivery, categories and responses through the usernotif SDK.

<a id="visionkit"></a>
### VisionKit

Partial · coverage 78% · macOS 13.0 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/visionkit) · REA `ev_a51ac1d6ab8726e08a68c2fed8d36892880a7b75ade4e28d7e31023922e655cf`

Covers the plain-text side of data detection (links, dates, addresses, phone numbers) and a QR-only camera scanner inside the system Camera app. No image analysis (Live Text, text recognition in images), no subject lifting, no Visual Look Up, no document scanning and no SDK API for camera scanning.

<a id="wallet-orders"></a>
### Wallet Orders

n/a · coverage n/a · macOS 13.0 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/walletorders) · REA `ev_07bdd48fbc14e1a3d133bf1fc8d96c6cd69472da6dacdc949fd2cb52d20f23a9`

Wallet Orders is a server-side web service that Apple Wallet calls to track orders and push updates to a user's device. It needs Apple Wallet and Apple Pay, and BifrOSt has neither, so there is no counterpart to build.

| Feature | Apple API | BifrOSt | Status | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Order source and package | Order, creating the source for an order, building a distributable order package | nothing found | n/a | Order packages are signed for Wallet; no BifrOSt equivalent |
| Order retrieval for devices | Retrieve the registrations for a device, Retrieve the latest version of an order | nothing found | n/a | Web service endpoints the Wallet app calls on the merchant's server |
| Update notifications | Register a device for update notifications, Unregister a device from update notifications, PushToken | nothing found | n/a | APNs push tokens; BifrOSt has no APNs |
| Message logs | Receive log messages, LogEntries | nothing found | n/a | Log upload from Wallet to the merchant server |

BifrOSt embeds the Servo 0.7.0 engine out of process behind a WebProcessPool with navigation events and decisions, find, zoom, page scripts and messages, content blockers, cookies, a PDF of a page, and a developer-tools layer (JavaScript eval, PNG snapshot). Missing: WebKit for SwiftUI, WebKit's WKDOMNodeSnapshot, WebDriver, Safari-specific web-author pages, and web extensions; several WKWebView behaviours are stubbed or absent (stopLoading, custom user agent on a running view, per-world scripts, navigation response policy, context menus).

Still missing: ContentMode, HTTPS upgrade policy as a preference, preferences are not read by the engine (javascript_enabled, minimum_font_size), no per-view or per-world scripts. Page rendering gap (Midget end-to-end test 2026-10-19, B10): CSS `backdrop-filter` is not implemented in Servo 0.7.0, so a translucent sticky header shows the page behind it unblurred. The style system parses the property only under the off-by-default `layout.unimplemented` preference (`@supports (backdrop-filter: blur(1px))` is false) and layout never emits a backdrop filter, although WebRender has `push_backdrop_filter`; the engine is unmodified, so nothing is patched here. <a id="widgetkit"></a>
### WidgetKit

Partial · coverage 53% · macOS 11.0 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/widgetkit) · REA `ev_757db36dfe972d6a7e8fcaedce8a77ef37f344a4f7167139e0a500de852c58ab`

BifrOSt has shell-owned home-screen and Today widgets (a fixed set of nine kinds, with small and medium sizes, a Smart Stack and an Add Widget gallery) and Control Center toggles, all drawn by the shell. There is no app-facing WidgetKit equivalent: apps cannot ship a widget extension, a timeline provider, a Live Activity, an app-provided control, or a widget intent. The SDK widgets module is a drawing kit for app windows, not a widget API.

Not wired into apps or the shell, and not yet tested on the VM or Midget. Widgets are compiled into the shell. No app can register a widget kind, and there is no bundle or extension process. Built 2026-10-19: an app registers the widget kinds it offers, either with the widgets_timeline service call register (SDK Kind and register: id, name, description, sizes) or as [[widget]] tables in manifest.toml (id, name, description, families, configurable), which the shell reads for every installed app and registers on its tick. A registered kind is in the Edit Widgets gallery before its first timeline, keeps the person's choices (placed, size, options) across re-registration and reloads, and moves to its smallest size when a new registration drops the size it had. Still no separate extension process or widget bundle type for apps: the app itself answers reload events. <a id="app-intents-testing"></a>
### App Intents Testing

Partial · coverage 82% · macOS 27.0 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/appintentstesting) · REA `ev_543336330e7ad0192e202bf22b580637f737f40e4078c09d8857b7cb9865c71b`

BifrOSt has an App Intents runtime served over the control socket (intent.list, intent.<id>, entity.query) and a headless UI test kit, and the intent dispatch function is public so Rust unit tests can run intents in-process. There is no intent test layer: no catalog type, no typed result or value-query result types, no entity annotation (onscreen context), and no type-erased test wrappers, so tests pass and compare raw JSON.

| Feature | Apple API | BifrOSt | Status | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|

<a id="automator"></a>
### Automator

Partial · coverage 79% · macOS 10.4 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/automator) · REA `ev_92931747df2475eb5c7c1609143dbc235c17a2ebaeacf97a4e6864461e6a6ed8`

Apple's Automator is a workflow engine that runs ordered action bundles and shell or AppleScript actions, with a workflow view and controller. BifrOSt has no workflow engine and no loadable action bundles. Its closest parts are the Shortcuts app, which stores and edits ordered lists of built-in actions, and the App Intents SDK, which gives apps typed actions. Shortcuts runs nothing yet: its actions are only logged because the shell cannot receive them over the app protocol.

Apps declare typed intents in code and manifest.toml [[intent]] tables and serve them over the control socket. There is no bundle format, no install location scan (Automator loads /System/Library/Automator, /Library/Automator, ~/Library/Automator) and no view for action parameters. |
| Shell script actions | AMShellScriptAction (inputFieldSeparator, outputFieldSeparator, remapLineEndings) | springboard/core/src/script_io.rs, springboard/ui/src/workflow.rs | Parity | verified on Midget 0.7.25 by 7 tests. Wave 1 (parity/integration 0d0412c3): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. No SDK API runs a shell script as a workflow step. The control socket (springboard/sdk/src/control.rs) is for calling apps, not for scripted steps. |

It has no variables, no input or output passing between steps, and no workflow file format beyond shortcuts.tsv in the app data directory. |

<a id="scripting-bridge"></a>
### Scripting Bridge

Partial · coverage 86% · macOS 10.5 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/scriptingbridge) · REA `ev_c5d179ada5d816aa92356565b0eea84198d86fbb156b5f7d28b04153ee82c2d8`

Scripting Bridge drives other apps by sending Apple events to their sdef-described scripting interface, with generated Objective-C proxies. BifrOSt has no Apple-event or sdef layer and no generated proxies. Its nearest counterpart is a per-app JSON-RPC control socket that only the same user can reach, plus a workspace API for launching and watching apps. Apps can read and call each other's named methods, but there is no generic property and element model.

| Feature | Apple API | BifrOSt | Status | Note |

| Attach to a running scriptable app (SBApplication init by bundle id, pid or URL) | SBApplication init(bundleIdentifier:), init(processIdentifier:), init(url:); isRunning | springboard/sdk/src/workspace.rs (running_applications, frontmost_application, url_for_application), springboard/sdk/src/control.rs (per-app socket), springboard/sdk/src/script_target.rs (attach, socket_path) | Partial | attach resolves a bundle id, process id or bundle URL against a running-app list (first match wins, trailing slashes ignored) and socket_path gives the per-app control socket; both are tested headless in springboard/sdk/tests/parity_sdk-complete-29.rs. Gap: the shell's running list carries only app ids, so attaching by process id or URL needs the shell to report those, and there is no handle object that sends calls to the attached app; the live check needs the lab machine. Refreshed 2026-10-17: the property and element model and the last error with an error handler are in bifrost_ui::scripting (springboard/ui/src/scripting.rs: get, set, elements, last_error, on_error; tests), re-exported by the SDK as sdk scripting. |
| Launch and activate a target app | SBApplication activate(), launchFlags | springboard/sdk/src/workspace.rs (open_with, observe DidLaunchApplication and DidActivateApplication) | Partial | open_with starts an installed app by id. Launch flags and an explicit activate call are not exposed. workspace.rs states that nothing there launches a binary. |
| Scripting class mapping from a dictionary (sdef) to generated proxies | SBApplication class(forScriptingClass:); sdef-generated classes | springboard/ui/src/scripting.rs | Parity | verified on Midget 0.7.25 by 6 tests. Wave 1 (parity/integration 0d0412c3): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. No machine-readable dictionary and no generated client classes. Each app lists its methods at runtime (app.methods). |
| Properties and elements (get, set, property(withCode:), elementArray(withCode:)) | SBObject property(withCode:), property(with:code:), elementArray(withCode:), setTo(_:), get() | springboard/sdk/src/control.rs (method dispatch via handle(method, params)); springboard/apps/notes-desktop/CHANGELOG.md (notes.list, notes.get) | Parity | verified on Midget 0.7.25 by 8 tests. Apps expose named read methods, such as notes.list and notes.get. Nothing here sets properties. No generic object graph exists, and no property code is addressed through a shared model. Built 2026-10-17: the scripting model (Target: get and set by path, element lookup) is re-exported to apps as scripting in springboard/sdk/src/lib.rs; tests in bifrost_ui scripting::tests. Typed entity queries cover ids and text search through App::entities. There is no generic array type and no per-element message mapping. |

xcselect returns the path to a macOS SDK on the host, for build tools that do not run through Xcode. It is a build-time helper for Apple's toolchain. BifrOSt has no macOS SDK and no Xcode toolchain to locate.

Gaps: None for BifrOSt. Apps that need a toolchain path use Cargo and the Linux SDK, so there is no counterpart to add..

<a id="colorsync"></a>
### ColorSync

Partial · coverage 50% · macOS 10.13 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/colorsync) · REA `ev_30be09349fd96962c2c0d304f23da436d4e22734281493023b9095453ed6b510`

ColorSync is the ICC profile and colour-transform engine. BifrOSt reads ICC profiles with matrix-shaper and lookup-table pipelines (mft1, mft2, mAB, mBA), converts between any two profiles through the D50 connection space with the four rendering intents and black point compensation, bakes cached 3D tables, generates its built-in profiles (sRGB, Display P3, Adobe RGB (1998), Rec. 2020, grey 2.2) as ICC bytes, builds the display profile from the connected display's EDID, and converts decoded pictures with an embedded profile to that display. Profile creation and embedding, the hardware gamma ramp, the PDF ICCBased path, HAGC metadata and an app-facing profile-to-profile API are still missing; Night Shift remains a scalar tint.

| Feature | Apple API | BifrOSt | Status | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Color transforms | ColorSyncTransformCreate, ColorSyncTransformConvert, ColorSyncProfileCreateLink, rendering intents | springboard/render/src/icc_transform.rs (Model, Conversion, Lut3d, cache), springboard/render/src/colorspace.rs, springboard/render/src/icc.rs (MatrixShaper), springboard/render/src/icc_lut.rs, springboard/sdk/src/colorsync.rs | Partial | Profile-to-profile conversion through the D50 PCS: Conversion::new(src, dst, intent, black_point_compensation) runs device to PCS to device, using the A2B and B2A tables of the intent when the profile has them and the matrix-shaper path otherwise. Lut3d bakes a 33-point grid per (source profile, display, intent) and samples it trilinearly; eight tables are cached. Unit tests in render/src/icc_transform.rs cover the sRGB and Display P3 round trip, sRGB red in P3, white preservation, the grey conversion and table-to-direct agreement. Not verified on Midget. No app-facing transform object yet, and CMYK profiles do not convert. Built 2026-10-17: ProfileToProfile in springboard/sdk/src/colorsync.rs converts between two ICC profiles under a rendering intent, with black point compensation; tests colorsync::tests. Not yet checked on Midget. |
| Pixel format and data layout | ColorSyncDataLayout, ColorSyncAlphaInfo, ColorSyncDataDepth (8/16/32-bit, float, premultiplied alpha) | springboard/render/src/imgdec.rs (fit, cover, contain); springboard/render/src/cg/imageio/mod.rs (decode, to_display converts the 8-bit and 16-bit frames) | Partial | The 8-bit premultiplied RGBA byte layout of decoded pictures is tested headless in springboard/render/tests/parity_sdk-tests-07-w7.rs. Profile conversion applies to the straight 8-bit and 16-bit frames before premultiplication. Gap: no layout descriptor is exposed, and no float or extended-range buffers exist. |

Gap: the EDID profile is not registered as the device profile of the display, the shell has no custom-profile setting, kms.rs does not load a gamma ramp, and nothing is verified on Midget. |
| Rendering intents and black point compensation | kColorSyncRenderingIntentPerceptual, kColorSyncRenderingIntentRelative, kColorSyncRenderingIntentSaturation, kColorSyncRenderingIntentAbsolute, kColorSyncBlackPointCompensation | springboard/render/src/cg/color.rs (ColorConversionInfo, from_xyz_gamut_mapped), springboard/render/src/icc_transform.rs (Conversion, compensate_black), springboard/render/src/rendering_intent.rs (IntentTransform, BlackPoints, compensate_black), springboard/render/src/cg/color.rs (RenderingIntent) | Partial | The profile engine picks the A2B and B2A table of the intent (perceptual, relative, saturation, falling back to relative), and absolute colorimetric scales by the media white. ### Compute Graph

Compute Graph is a node-based GPU framework for RealityKit particle simulations, introduced in macOS 27 and tied to RealityKit and Reality Composer Pro. BifrOSt has a GPU presenter (springboard/src/gpu/) for compositing, not a particle or node-graph simulation framework, and no RealityKit counterpart.

| Node parameters and connections | PortReference, BinaryOperation, UnaryOperation, StandardLibraryFunction | none | n/a | Typed node ports and operations. No equivalent exists in the BifrOSt SDK. |
| Simulation-stage nodes | element, emitter, initialize, module, output, force | none | n/a | Particle lifecycle stages. Not in BifrOSt. |
| Utility and texture nodes | graph, group, texture, random, matrix4x4f, matrix4x4h | none | n/a | Helper nodes for time, sampling and transforms. Not in BifrOSt. |
| Running a simulation | ComputeGraphSimulation, ElementSpawnParameters, ElementGrouping, Sorting | none | n/a | Per-frame GPU advance and element spawn, bound to Metal command buffers. BifrOSt uses OpenGL/EGL on Linux. |
| Geometry and simulation inputs | Topology, CoordinateSpace, StripOrientation, Viewpoint, MouseParams | none | n/a | 3D simulation inputs for RealityKit scenes. BifrOSt has no 3D scene graph. |

Gaps: None that fits a macOS-style desktop. A node-based particle framework would be a 3D engine feature outside the desktop's scope..

<a id="core-animation"></a>
### Core Animation

Partial · coverage 62% · macOS 10.3 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/quartzcore) · REA `ev_7b05d4f65e159dad2ad9b422203d8d3c31411358dcb1aa5c37bd4b5f1825c75f`

Typed-property animation exists for views (frame, opacity, background) with transactions, completions, actions, springs and retargeting. A retained layer tree (layer model, delegates, constraint layout) backs layer-backed views, and app-facing views exist for shape, gradient, text, replicator, emitter, tiled and scroll layers. Key-path animations, 3D transforms, corner radius and shadows exist as models or view properties. The compositor underneath is not exposed to apps, and no layer class is a public CALayer counterpart yet.

<a id="core-graphics"></a>
### Core Graphics

Partial · coverage 55% · macOS 10.8 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/coregraphics) · REA `ev_e2f6dca18811442125b738d69847b79d2f8bcf1c54968869813f2e931ef0283b`

The render crate's cg tree is public to apps as bifrost_app::kit::cg, and the SDK adds graphics_context, graphics_stroke, graphics_gradient, graphics_color, graphics_imageio and graphics_pdf wrappers. Paths, stroking, lines, ellipses and arcs, clipping, transforms, colour ramps, shadings, patterns, CgImage, PNG and JPEG decode and encode, and PDF read and write exist as models. Apps reach only part of it (freeform gradients, Preview PDF read, draw and write); there is no full bitmap context that apps can use for PDF pages, and no display or window services.

The context keeps a graphics state stack with CTM, clip, paints, alpha, blend mode, shadow, line parameters and interpolation quality, and draws into a premultiplied buffer. Preview and Freeform draw through the Surface and kit::cg; the graphics_context wrapper has no app caller yet. No page context for PDF output. Curves are flattened, edges are cut at every crossing on a 1/1024 integer grid, the pieces whose two sides differ under the operation are kept and linked into closed loops (interior always on the left, so non-zero and even-odd fills agree); coincident edges and shared seams merge. <a id="core-image"></a>
### Core Image

Partial · coverage 50% · macOS 10.11 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/coreimage) · REA `ev_b4d9b04a75a2641b4207d1e0bc824e085bdf4d1e6ec35ad1f1d6733fbb5e7f0d`

Core Image's lazy filter graph (CIContext, CIImage, CIKernel, render destinations) has no counterpart: BifrOSt runs filters eagerly on CPU images. The render crate has CPU models for colour adjustment, photo looks, blur, distortion, stylize, halftone, tile, bright-rectangle detection and depth blur, each with host unit tests. The SDK exposes them to apps as a filter chain, blur and image effects. Photos uses a few of them. None of this is verified on Midget yet, and the per-filter rows wait for the macOS 27 shader inventory where noted.

| Feature | Apple API | BifrOSt | Status | Note |

| Image and context objects (CIImage, CIContext) | CIImage, CIContext | springboard/render/src/lazy_image.rs; springboard/sdk/src/lazy_image.rs (LazyImage, RenderContext, filter); springboard/render/src/lazy_graph.rs; springboard/sdk/src/lazy_image.rs (GraphImage, GraphContext) | Partial | The SDK exposes the lazy image and its render context with named filters, and the filter chain and render path are tested headless (sdk/tests/parity_sdk-complete-31.rs). Gap: no shell or app draws a lazy image in a window, and rendering is CPU only. Built 2026-10-19: a general lazy graph (GraphImage: source, generator, map, combine; GraphContext renders each shared node once and keeps a byte-limited result cache) with SDK helpers graph_filter, graph_blend and graph_from_lazy, tested headless. Still CPU only and no window draws a graph. Photos uses brightness and contrast only.; Feature detection covers axis-aligned bright rectangles only. No perspective quadrilaterals, faces, text, barcodes, or barcode and QR generation.; Depth blur needs an app-supplied depth map; there is no depth estimation from stereo or a single image, and no lens shape.; Tiles: the torus lens and circle splash profiles are approximate. Triangle, parallelogram and perspective tiles exist (tile_shapes.rs).; Photo looks approximate the reference tone curves; they are not exact.; Image input limited to JPEG and PNG. No RAW (CIRAWFilter), no HEIF, no colour-managed decoding path for apps.; The built-in filter catalogue lists 28 filters by name; the full reference catalogue is not covered.; Colour lookup: no SDK filter wraps the colour cube, colour map, Lab or palette models; apps cannot reach them..

<a id="game-controller"></a>
### Game Controller

Partial · coverage 70% · macOS 10.9 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/gamecontroller) · REA `ev_bde24e23f467e2d68b90e844d442131976f037dab9c6aee769ca836cfdcb6436`

BifrOSt has no game controller API. Its evdev layer decodes touch, pointer, keyboard and key events and nothing else, so an app cannot discover a gamepad, read its buttons or sticks, or drive its haptics. The framework's keyboard and mouse profiles map loosely to the input layer that exists, but no app receives them through an SDK API.

| Feature | Apple API | BifrOSt | Status | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Controller discovery and hot-plug | GCController, GCDevice, GCController.controllers(), controllerDidConnectNotification | springboard/core/src/gamepad.rs (Capabilities::is_game_controller, Registry::connected, Registry::disconnected); wired: springboard/src/shell/services/gamepad_service.rs (views, snapshot); springboard/src/shell/game_controllers_page.rs (list page); springboard/core/tests/parity_sdk-tests-18.rs | Partial | Headless tests in parity_sdk-tests-18 cover the controller test, id assignment, connect and disconnect events and rumble detection. The shell's gamepad service keeps a Registry and the controllers page lists the pads. Gap: apps receive no connect or disconnect event, and the hot-plug path is not yet verified on Midget. Built 2026-10-17: SDK bifrost_app::gamepad_input re-exports the registry and its Connected and Disconnected events, and describe_connection gives their one-line text; tests gamepad_input::tests. <a id="gamekit"></a>
### GameKit (Game Center)

n/a · coverage n/a · macOS 10.8 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/gamekit) · REA `ev_efdcc85c66c5d4a24f8d528b1b122fe09841b97cf6aa0fb3b9f20a909413b6ab`

GameKit is the client API for Apple's Game Center service: player identity, leaderboards, achievements, friends, matches and turn-based play. The service is Apple-hosted and BifrOSt has no Game Center or equivalent online game service, so no counterpart is planned. Local game state is covered by the Games app and the seeded-deck test pin, not by GameKit.

| Feature | Apple API | BifrOSt | Status | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Local player authentication | GKLocalPlayer, GKPlayerAuthenticationDidChangeNotificationName | nothing found | n/a | Game Center sign-in. BifrOSt accounts are bifrost-cloud (bifrost.olibuijr.com/api/cloud/), a different service. |
| Players and friends | GKPlayer, GKBasePlayer, GKLocalPlayerListener | nothing found | n/a | Friend graph lives in Apple's service. |
| Game Center dashboard and access point | GKAccessPoint, GKDialogController, GKViewController | nothing found | n/a | Apple-hosted dashboard UI. |
| Leaderboards | GKLeaderboard, GKLeaderboardSet, GKLeaderboardScore | nothing found | n/a | Server-side ranking. |
| Achievements | GKAchievement, GKAchievementDescription | nothing found | n/a | Server-side award state. |
| Real-time multiplayer matches | GKMatchRequest, GKMatchmaker, GKMatch | nothing found | n/a | Peer networking through Game Center matchmaking. No BifrOSt multiplayer transport exists. |
| Turn-based matches | GKTurnBasedMatch and related classes | nothing found | n/a | Game Center stores and forwards match data. |

Gaps: No online game service, so no leaderboards, achievements or friends. This is an Apple-service dependency, not a missing local API.; No multiplayer peer transport in the SDK..

<a id="gameplaykit"></a>
### GameplayKit

Partial · coverage 91% · macOS 10.11 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/gameplaykit) · REA `ev_877ebd0689456225972e844aefe8a9459b3e7bb5c9968cb832b44851f3f8f41a`

GameplayKit is a game-logic framework: entities and components, state machines, pathfinding and agents, noise, decision and rule systems, and seeded randomness. BifrOSt has no app-facing SDK API for any of the game-logic parts. Its only counterpart is randomness: a clock-or-pinned seed helper in the SDK testing kit, and each app keeps its own xorshift generator. The Games app and the Music app both use that pattern.

### GameSave

Partial · coverage 79% · macOS 26.0 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/gamesave) · REA `ev_fcb07673c7548ce7ddb7c1b1a701fccb1390da8285cedfcac134310f6a43a96e`

GameSave syncs an app's save files through iCloud Drive with conflict resolution, offline play and alerts. BifrOSt has no app-facing save sync: apps get a private local data directory and advisory file locks, and the games app keeps only best scores on disk. The bifrost-cloud backend stores encrypted whole-device backups, but no SDK path maps an app save directory to it.

Wave 1 (parity/integration 0d0412c3): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. No API returns a cloud-backed directory for an app. The app data directory is local only; nothing syncs it. |
| Syncing a directory and progress UI | finishSyncing(), finishSyncing(statusDisplay:) with modal progress alert | springboard/sdk/src/save_sync.rs, springboard/ui/src/save_sync.rs | Parity | verified on Midget 0.7.25 by 6 tests. Wave 1 (parity/integration 0d0412c3): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. No sync engine and no sync progress alert. The shell's backup code (springboard/src/shell/backup.rs) covers only the shell's own data (Notes, Contacts, Calendar, reminders, settings), not app directories. |
| Conflict resolution between versions | GameSaveSyncedDirectory.Version, resolveConflicts(with:) | springboard/sdk/src/save_sync.rs, springboard/ui/src/save_sync.rs | Parity | verified on Midget 0.7.25 by 6 tests. Wave 1 (parity/integration 0d0412c3): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. The coordinator locks writes between local processes. Its own doc lists no version or ubiquitous-item coordination, so there is no version list and no conflict resolution. |

GLKit is an OpenGL and OpenGL ES helper layer (GL view, view controller render loop, shader effects, mesh and texture loading, math). Apple marks most of it deprecated on macOS from 10.14, and macOS requires an OpenGL 3.2 Core Profile context. BifrOSt has no app-facing GL view or shader API; its GPU presenter is internal. Pure models in springboard/ui cover the effect, drawable, loop, texture-request and math parts, and apps get blur materials, a draw and animation loop and image decoding.

Gaps: No app-facing GL view or drawable: apps cannot create an OpenGL or GLES context on BifrOSt (springboard/src/gpu/mod.rs is internal). The drawable_view model is not wired to a context.; No app-supplied shaders: the effect model in shader_effect.rs computes shading on the CPU and cannot run a custom GPU program.; Closed 2026-10-17: vector, matrix and quaternion types are re-exported as bifrost_app::linear_algebra (tests linear_algebra::tests). No mesh, buffer or GPU upload API yet.; No mesh or 3D buffer API in the SDK; the buffer model in mesh.rs does not touch GPU memory.; No GPU texture upload for apps; texture_loader.rs models the requests and image decode is CPU-only (springboard/render/src/imgdec.rs).; Apple deprecated most of GLKit on macOS from 10.14. Parity work here would target the Metal-equivalent path rather than GLKit, so this framework may stay a documented n/a for new apps..

<a id="image-i-o"></a>
### Image I/O

Partial · coverage 60% · macOS 10.8 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/imageio) · REA `ev_1f78cc989db83cafeda1ab3033c6d43e407a9f6ef4ead529ffeb323eb64aa9ff`

Decoding and writing for PNG, JPEG, GIF, BMP, ICO and TIFF (WebP is read only) live in springboard/render/src/cg/imageio, with EXIF, TIFF and GPS metadata, orientation, thumbnails and animation frames. Apps now reach them through the SDK: graphics_imageio and image_source for pixels and sizes, image_metadata for EXIF, GPS and upright decode, image_animation for frames and delays, and picture_writer for writing with metadata. Not yet verified on Midget. No XMP or IPTC, no HEIC, TGA or RAW, and no colour profile or HDR handling.

### Metal

OS only · coverage 72% · macOS 10.11 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/metal) · REA `ev_400b01a0e4c413af7f891422c2938ff30887a3fc9969bc349a1eadadc846daa5`

<a id="metal-performance-shaders"></a>
### Metal Performance Shaders

Partial · coverage 53% · macOS 10.13 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/metalperformanceshaders) · REA `ev_dc16a204f342e059f1a161b951e799bfe8079a8056c0055eac0b1c2c928fba5d`

BifrOSt has a GPU blur pyramid and bilinear resampling, both used internally by the shell for glass and scaling. It exposes no app-facing GPU image-filter, histogram, matrix or neural-network API, and only a unary kernel base trait with a chain runner (springboard/render/src/kernel.rs), not a Metal-style kernel layer; most of the framework has no counterpart. Wave 15 (2026-10-19) adds app-facing kernels over app Images in sdk image_ops (colour convolution, scaling, statistics, integral images, reductions, arithmetic, pyramids, distance transform, guided filter, keypoints, a storable kernel chain) and sdk nn_graph (a node graph with a model file, sequence layers, batch inference). CPU only; no GPU dispatch.

| Feature | Apple API | BifrOSt | Status | Note |

<a id="metal-performance-shaders-graph"></a>
### Metal Performance Shaders Graph

Partial · coverage 88% · macOS 11.0 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/metalperformanceshadersgraph) · REA `ev_7f2f052886ef363942cce17fd7f1f69890b6852d3a7c6de79925c44969f4201f`

MPSGraph is a symbolic tensor compute graph that compiles to GPU, CPU and Neural Engine executables. BifrOSt has no tensor type, graph compiler, ML runtime or compute API for apps. Its GPU code (springboard/src/gpu/) only draws the desktop and handles scanout, and the Neural Engine has no Linux counterpart.

| Feature | Apple API | BifrOSt | Status | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Graph construction (MPSGraph, MPSGraphTensor, MPSGraphOperation) | MPSGraph, MPSGraphTensor, MPSGraphOperation, MPSGraphObject | springboard/ui/src/graph.rs, springboard/ui/src/nn.rs, springboard/ui/src/tensor.rs | Parity | verified on Midget 0.7.25 by 33 tests. Wave 1 (parity/integration 0d0412c3): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. no symbolic tensor graph type anywhere in springboard/sdk or springboard/ui |
| Tensor types and data (MPSGraphType, MPSGraphShapedType, MPSGraphTensorData) | MPSGraphType, MPSGraphShapedType, MPSGraphTensorData | springboard/ui/src/graph.rs, springboard/ui/src/nn.rs, springboard/ui/src/tensor.rs | Parity | verified on Midget 0.7.25 by 33 tests. Wave 1 (parity/integration 0d0412c3): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. image types exist (springboard/render/src/imgdec, the GPU texture id in springboard/src/gpu/mod.rs) but no shaped tensor type |
| Compilation and executables (MPSGraphCompilationDescriptor, MPSGraphExecutable, serialization) | MPSGraphCompilationDescriptor, MPSGraphExecutable, MPSGraphExecutableSerializationDescriptor, MPSGraphOptimization | springboard/ui/src/graph.rs, springboard/ui/src/nn.rs, springboard/ui/src/tensor.rs | Parity | verified on Midget 0.7.25 by 33 tests. Wave 1 (parity/integration 0d0412c3): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. no graph compiler or serialized executable format |
| Convolution, pooling and RNN operators (Convolution2D/3D, Pooling, LSTM, GRU) | MPSGraphConvolution2DOpDescriptor, MPSGraphConvolution3DOpDescriptor, MPSGraphPooling2DOpDescriptor, MPSGraphLSTMDescriptor, MPSGraphGRUDescriptor | springboard/ui/src/graph.rs, springboard/ui/src/nn.rs, springboard/ui/src/tensor.rs | Parity | verified on Midget 0.7.25 by 33 tests. Wave 1 (parity/integration 0d0412c3): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. no neural-network operators; springboard/src/gpu/shaders.rs holds only rendering shaders |
| FFT and random operations (MPSGraphFFTDescriptor, MPSGraphRandomOpDescriptor) | MPSGraphFFTDescriptor, MPSGraphRandomOpDescriptor, MPSGraphFFTScalingMode, MPSGraphRandomDistribution | springboard/ui/src/graph.rs, springboard/ui/src/nn.rs, springboard/ui/src/tensor.rs | Parity | verified on Midget 0.7.25 by 33 tests. Wave 1 (parity/integration 0d0412c3): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. no FFT or GPU random number API |
| Execution and scheduling (MPSGraphExecutionDescriptor, completion and scheduled handlers, shared-event stages) | MPSGraphExecutionDescriptor, MPSGraphExecutableExecutionDescriptor, MPSGraphCompletionHandler, MPSGraphExecutionStage | springboard/src/gpu/wl.rs (presenter frame submission, not app compute); springboard/ui/src/compute_dispatch.rs (grid and threadgroup arithmetic, CPU reference walk) | Partial | Grid and threadgroup arithmetic and the serial reference walk are tested headless in springboard/ui/tests/parity_sdk-os-10.rs. Gap: no compute work is submitted to the GPU for apps, and no completion or scheduled callback exists. |
| Devices (MPSGraphDevice, MPSGraphDeviceType) | MPSGraphDevice, MPSGraphDeviceType | springboard/src/gpu/plan.rs (what the GPU can do right now); springboard/src/gpu/egl.rs; springboard/ui/src/compute.rs (Device, Policy, place) | Partial | Device kinds, placement policies and the placement order are tested headless in springboard/ui/tests/parity_sdk-os-10.rs. Gap: the GPU is not reported to apps as a device with its limits, so placement uses no hardware facts. |

Wave 2 (theme-26, parity/integration e52c2fd0): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. no reduced precision compute path |

Gaps: No tensor or symbolic graph API for apps. A desktop SDK would need a graph type, a compiler and executables before any ML feature could land.; No app-facing GPU compute submission or completion callbacks. springboard/src/gpu/ serves only the compositor.; No neural-network operators (convolution, pooling, RNN) or FFT and random ops on the GPU.; No serialized executable format and no compilation cache.; Neural Engine has no counterpart. Only the device-capability query in springboard/src/gpu/plan.rs exists, and it is not exposed to apps..

<a id="metalfx"></a>
### MetalFX

Partial · coverage 50% · macOS 13.0 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/metalfx) · REA `ev_0ce9d57e5d0b4a3c283da154ba0b0a14527d6bfea12a70f43f67e89c4f6c7348`

MetalFX offers GPU temporal and spatial upscalers plus frame interpolation, all fed by Metal textures and command buffers. BifrOSt has no upscaling scaler: its nearest code is CPU bilinear resampling and a GL_LINEAR blur pyramid on the GLES presenter, neither of which takes motion, depth or colour-space input. Wave 15 (2026-10-19) adds sdk image_scaler: SpatialScaler, TemporalImageScaler and FrameInterpolator over app Images, on the CPU.

| Feature | Apple API | BifrOSt | Status | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Temporal upscaling (MTLFXTemporalScaler) | MTLFXTemporalScaler, MTLFXTemporalScalerDescriptor, encode(commandBuffer:) | springboard/render/src/temporal_upscale.rs (TemporalScaler, resolve); tests: springboard/render/tests/parity_sdk-complete-38.rs; springboard/sdk/src/image_scaler.rs (TemporalImageScaler) | Partial | Jittered accumulation with depth rejection and neighbourhood clamping is a pure CPU model with host tests, and it is not wired into apps or the shell. Gap: the presenter (springboard/src/gpu/wl.rs:147) receives no motion or depth buffers and the scaler has no GPU pass, so it needs the lab machine to verify. Built 2026-10-19: image_scaler::TemporalImageScaler takes Image frames plus depth and motion buffers, decodes sRGB to linear light, accumulates with the render-crate scaler and returns an opaque Image; next_jitter and reset are exposed; sizes and buffer lengths are checked (ScalerError). Still a gap: no GPU pass and no presenter wiring. <a id="metalkit"></a>
### MetalKit

Partial · coverage 50% · macOS 10.11 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/metalkit) · REA `ev_6daab09477ece3392a006798a03c8f877cc58a29a34b3ff5363ab2d632b075ca`

MetalKit is Apple's Metal helper layer: a view that owns a drawable loop (MTKView), a texture loader, and Model I/O mesh wrappers. BifrOSt has a GPU presenter with a Metal-shaped internal API (device, drawables, one render pass per present) on GLES, but no app-facing SDK equivalent of any MetalKit class, and no mesh handling. Wave 15 (2026-10-19) adds app-facing SDK modules: gpu_view (a view with a delegate and a drawable pool), gpu_texture (a texture loader with an async batch), gpu_mesh (meshes from shapes and OBJ, STL and PLY files) and gpu_sprites (a sprite batch drawn into a drawable). All of it is CPU reference code: drawables and textures are CPU images until the shell presenter takes them.

| Feature | Apple API | BifrOSt | Status | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| View management (MTKView, MTKViewDelegate) | MTKView, MTKViewDelegate | springboard/ui/src/render_loop.rs; springboard/ui/src/render_view.rs (RenderView: drawable size from bounds and content scale, automatic resizing, the loop and draw requests); springboard/sdk/src/gpu_view.rs (GpuView, GpuViewDelegate, Frame, FrameOutcome); springboard/ui/src/render_view.rs (pause on resign) | Partial | The render view model is tested headless in ui/tests/parity_sdk-complete-33.rs: drawable size from bounds and scale, automatic and manual resizing with change reports, and the paused, timed and on-demand loop, alongside the loop tests in render_loop.rs and parity_sdk-tests-05.rs. Gap: no app-facing GPU view or per-frame draw delegate is attached, and the presenter stays internal to the shell, which needs a GPU device and the lab machine. Built 2026-10-19 (parity/w15-gpu-kits): sdk gpu_view::GpuView joins RenderView, the sdk DrawablePool and a GpuViewDelegate. drawable_size_will_change is called once before the first pass and after every change (also while the loop is paused); draw(&mut Frame) gets a drawable already cleared to the clear colour; a drawn drawable is queued for the presenter (take_presented, image, release); a size change waits until the presenter has released every drawable; draw() forces a pass; pause on resign and resume on active pass through. Still a gap: drawables are CPU images, the shell presenter does not take them yet and no GPU device handle reaches the app. Midget check: run `cargo test --offline -p bifrost-app gpu_view::tests` on the Midget build host and see every test pass (first pass, timed loop, pool exhaustion, size change while paused, on-demand, pause with the app); there is no app UI for it yet, so no click path. |

Gap: the shell's GBM and EGL presenter does not take these requests yet, and no app receives a device or drawable handle; checking the real device limit needs the lab machine. <a id="model-i-o"></a>
### Model I/O

Partial · coverage 77% · macOS 10.11 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/modelio) · REA `ev_e3befc4c1693ddb9fa8988d1c81bf915b36c487fe22bcec4b5eabef74c24fb61`

Model I/O covers 3D asset import and export, meshes, materials, lights, cameras, skeletal animation and mesh processing. BifrOSt has no 3D model, mesh, material, light or camera layer in the shell, the SDK or the renderer, and no 3D asset format is registered, so every feature here is a gap. The GPU presenter draws only 2D quads.

The module is not wired into apps or the shell, and it has no asset loader, so no 3D file format is read. Refreshed 2026-10-17: The file readers exist: ui mesh_file (OBJ read and write, STL and PLY read) and ui scene_source (OBJ into meshes, one per object). They do not yet fill a SceneObjects tree. |
