Gap: no renderer consumes the transform stack, and the rotate, scale and translate forms are one enum rather than separate types. |

Gaps: No general app-facing PDFPage or PDFView object: sdk peek_pdf::PdfPreview wraps the PDFView model for the Peek app only. graphics_pdf::Document has open, page count and size, render, outline, find and page text.; No annotation objects read from or written to PDF files: ui/src/annotation.rs is an in-memory model. No widget or AcroForm support.; No PDFThumbnailView and no page drawing into an app-provided context; ui pdfpage gives thumbnail_size and fit_transform only.; No text selection in PDFs (PDFSelection); find returns page indexes, not ranges of text.; No write path for existing files: graphics_pdf's writer builds new files from drawn pages, but Save as PDF copies the original file, so page edits, rotation and password handling cannot be written.; Printing sends the file to CUPS unchanged; page ranges are set in the shell's print sheet (ui print_ranges.rs), but there is no pagination of PDF content (see docs/bifrost-ui.md:1322-1333).

<a id="pencilkit"></a>
### PencilKit

Partial · coverage 50% · macOS 10.15 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/pencilkit) · REA `ev_d8cb7973764b54aa73ace7b160012147dcb953f7ba035402f0e5962ec1621650`

BifrOSt has two working drawing surfaces: the shell's screenshot markup editor (pen, marker, pencil, eraser, undo, PNG save) and the Freeform app (pen, marker, eraser, palette, undo, PNG save). Neither is exposed to apps through the SDK. The ui crate holds pure models for a stroke and drawing data model with a text save format, stroke-level erasing, lasso selection, handwriting line segmentation with a recogniser hook, and Scribble gesture resolution. Since 2026-10-19 the SDK also has the canvas view (bifrost_app::canvas_view::CanvasView: pointer, touch and stylus input, tools, undo, lasso, save and load, render). No shell app uses it yet, there is no handwriting recogniser, and the compositor does not deliver pen-tablet pressure and tilt to apps.

| Feature | Apple API | BifrOSt | Status | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Canvas view capturing pen and finger input | PKCanvasView | springboard/sdk/src/canvas_view.rs (CanvasView); springboard/src/shell/markup.rs (Markup::touch, line 162); springboard/tests/parity_sdk-tests-05.rs; springboard/apps/freeform-desktop/src/freeform.rs; wired: springboard/apps/notes-desktop/src/notes/mod.rs (sketch_touch, draw_sketch) | Partial | Both capture Down/Move/Up touch events and stamp strokes onto a pixel buffer. The markup editor's touch path is tested headless in springboard/tests/parity_sdk-tests-05.rs: a press stamps a dot, a drag inks a line, and touches outside the picture draw nothing. 2026-10-19: the SDK view is built, bifrost_app::canvas_view::CanvasView: it takes the app's touch frames (touches: a mouse or trackpad is an indirect touch, a stylus a pencil touch with force) and raw digitizer reports (stylus), builds strokes with the picker's ink (kind, colour, width) and each point's time, force and tilt, erases (vector and bitmap), lasso-selects and moves strokes, keeps 100 undo levels, saves and loads (data_representation, set_drawing_data), maps zoom and offset, and renders the drawing plus the live stroke (render_view). Drawing policy (DrawingPolicy Default/AnyInput/PencilOnly): on the desktop form factor every input draws and a pen alone never turns fingers off, a mouse is never refused; a finger is refused only on a tablet after a pencil was seen, or under PencilOnly. Tests: sdk/src/canvas_view.rs tests (a_mouse_drag_draws_one_stroke_with_the_selected_ink, the_policy_decides_which_inputs_draw, on_a_tablet_the_default_policy_turns_fingers_off_once_a_pencil_is_seen, a_pen_tablet_stroke_keeps_pressure_and_tilt_and_a_hover_ends_it, a_stroke_stops_growing_at_the_point_limit, hostile data and locations). Not built: no app uses the view yet (Notes' sketch pad, Freeform and the shell markup keep their own stroke code); the compositor does not deliver tablet-tool events (pressure, tilt) to apps, so on the PC a pen is a pointer without pressure; no scroll view. ### Quartz

Partial · coverage 57% · macOS 10.4 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/quartz) · REA `ev_785e790b371318807d1dd7aa7f8f22ed4ec659d31eb5ce193106fc12c14d19a5`

BifrOSt covers the viewing and editing side of ImageKit only inside shell apps (Photos viewer, edit mode and slideshow), a Quick Look preview model and thumbnail cache in the SDK, PDF reading and writing through the SDK document and writer wrappers, PNG and JPEG decode and encode, and PDF text extraction for Books. A pure typed DAG model now covers part of Quartz Composer; there is still no composition UI, renderer or plug-in host. No app-facing SDK API exists yet for image views, slideshows, Core Image filters, PDF outlines or selections.

### RealityKit

RealityKit is an AR-first 3D simulation and rendering framework for Apple platforms, built around ARKit anchors, visionOS immersive spaces and Reality Composer Pro assets. BifrOSt is a 2D macOS-style desktop with no AR, spatial or 3D scene layer, so there is no counterpart to map.

| AR anchors and presentation | Anchors, Views and attachments, Presentation UI | none | n/a | No AR tracking or camera-anchored content on BifrOSt. |
| Physics and collision | Collision detection, Simulations and motion, Physics joints and pins | none | n/a | No physics engine in the desktop stack. |
| Navigation meshes | NavigationMeshComponent, NavigationController | none | n/a | Not applicable to a 2D desktop. |

Gaps: No 3D scene or entity layer in the SDK; No AR or spatial anchoring; the platform does not target visionOS or ARKit-class hardware.

### SceneKit

Partial · coverage 69% · macOS 10.8 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/scenekit) · REA `ev_264767f12439dbf1103290ef90b074174ebee91d7df825b31e986dca6396794a`

SceneKit is a 3D scene graph (nodes, cameras, lights, materials, geometry, physics, particles, audio, shaders). BifrOSt has no 3D scene, mesh or camera type anywhere in the SDK, UI or render crates; its rendering is 2D. Apple deprecated SceneKit in favour of RealityKit, so a 3D gap is expected on a 2D macOS-style desktop and most rows are n/a or gap.

<a id="audio-unit"></a>
### Audio Unit

Partial · coverage 56% · macOS 10.0 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/audiounit) · REA `ev_3bf9c005e0da939facd73989466bcbdab9f09176783e42e4aeed3b6e830276e4`

Apple's Audio Unit framework hosts third-party AU v2 and v3 plug-ins and provides the AUAudioUnit subclassing API for plug-in extensions. BifrOSt has a plug-in host model and an extension point model (manifests, a registry and render-resource allocation), and since 2026-10-19 an in-process loader for third-party units over its own C ABI (springboard/audio/units/src/plugin.rs), a sample-accurate sequencer unit and a General MIDI synth, but no AU binary compatibility and no separate extension process. The DAW ships its own built-in instruments and effects as JavaScript plug-in directories, which are not Audio Units. The Apple page itself marks the framework as deprecated in favour of Audio Toolbox.

| Feature | Apple API | BifrOSt | Status | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Hosting third-party AU v2 and v3 plug-ins | AUAudioUnit, AudioUnit instantiation (Audio Unit framework landing page) | springboard/ui/src/plugin_host.rs (Instance, Instance::new, PluginVersion); springboard/ui/tests/parity_sdk-complete-43.rs; springboard/audio/units/src/plugin.rs (PluginLibrary::open, PluginUnit, scan_directory); springboard/audio/units/examples/gain_plugin.c; springboard/cmd/src/unitctl.rs (bifrost-unit scan) | Partial | Built 2026-10-19 (written without a build, tests unrun): an in-process plug-in loader. A shared library exports bifrost_unit_entry, which returns a C ABI table (UnitVTable, version 1); PluginLibrary::open dlopens it, reads the component description and parameters, and instantiate() gives a PluginUnit that is an ordinary AudioUnit (it goes in a UnitHost, an engine node or the out-of-process Worker). The host owns the parameter ramps (the plug-in gets param_start and param_end each block), MIDI arrives at frame offsets, render allocates nothing, and non-finite output is silenced. register_into adds the plug-in to the ComponentRegistry and scan_directory loads /usr/lib/bifrost/units and ~/.local/share/bifrost/units. Unit tests use in-process tables and a real dlopen of libm. The ABI is ours (no AU v2 or v3 binary compatibility) and no separate extension process is started; the DAW rack does not load plug-ins yet. Midget check: build the C example on Titan (same x86_64): `cc -shared -fPIC -O2 -o cgain.so springboard/audio/units/examples/gain_plugin.c`, copy cgain.so to Midget, run `bifrost-unit scan .` (expect `C Gain  effect  aufx/cgan/test  up to 2 channels  1 parameter` and a line for parameter 0 Main/Gain), then `bifrost-unit render ./cgain.so /tmp/g.wav` (peak 0.500) and `bifrost-unit render ./cgain.so --set 0=2 /tmp/g2.wav` (peak 1.000). |

<a id="avfaudio"></a>
### AVFAudio

Partial · coverage 54% · macOS 11.3 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/avfaudio) · REA `ev_df0e56197670a298d99ca1c65c39630cfb6848bc2d4d337b0ef4e4f301f36f1d`

BifrOSt has a system audio service (audiod) that owns the speaker and microphone, with playback queue, volume, mute and WAV recording exposed to apps through the SDK audio client. App-level permission and input mute, player pan, rate and volume fades are modelled in the SDK; session categories, interruptions and route notifications are modelled but not wired to audiod. The AVAudioEngine graph and MIDI playback have no full app-facing counterpart; speech synthesis is app-facing through the shell speech service (espeak-ng) but partial; the output route is switched by the shell alone.

Category, mode, options, activation and interruptions are still the local pure model, not arbitrated in audiod. <a id="avrouting"></a>
### AVRouting

Partial · coverage 81% · macOS 13.0 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/avrouting) · REA `ev_14110f8179b556b56f5de61c07bede4c7dfac89ff255facccf244207b2b7d697`

AVRouting lets an app add third-party media receivers to the system route picker (AirPlay-style) through custom routing controllers, routing events and action items, and arbitrates playback between participants. BifrOSt has pure models for route rows, authorization, events, arbitration and a receiver-discovery feed, but no running network browse service or shell receiver picker; the audio layer also switches local speaker/headphone output.

Cinematic reads and edits depth-of-field video recorded by Apple's Cinematic mode, which needs Apple camera hardware and the Camera app's asset format. BifrOSt has no counterpart for that capture format, so the framework does not apply.

| Feature | Apple API | BifrOSt | Status | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Playing and editing Cinematic mode video | CNScript, CNDecision, CNDetectionTrack | nothing found | n/a | depends on Cinematic-mode asset files with focus metadata |
| Reading and rendering Cinematic assets | CNAssetInfo, CNCompositionInfo, CNRenderingSession | nothing found | n/a | Apple asset format only |
| Editing Spatial Audio with an audio mix | CNAssetSpatialAudioInfo, CNSpatialAudioRenderingStyle | springboard/audiod (plain speaker and microphone service) | n/a | no spatial audio mix for Cinematic assets |
| Detection and focus decisions | CNDetection, CNDecision, CNDetectionType | nothing found | n/a | face, torso and pet detections come from Cinematic metadata |
| Custom object tracking | CNObjectTracker, CNBoundsPrediction | nothing found | n/a | no tracker in the shell or SDK |
| Still-image shallow depth of field | CNImageRenderingSession, CNImageRenderingSessionConfiguration | springboard/apps/photocraft-desktop (photo app, no depth-of-field rendering found) | n/a | Metal-based SDoF rendering with no BifrOSt counterpart |

Gaps: Cinematic-mode asset reading and editing: no Apple Cinematic metadata or asset format on BifrOSt; Depth-of-field and focus-point rendering on video or stills.

<a id="core-audio"></a>
### Core Audio

Partial · coverage 64% · macOS 10.0 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/coreaudio) · REA `ev_bd10e360fb1e915d03b738fad1e0a829b4d87a74e798502bbe22e6d509ce6332`

BifrOSt covers speaker playback, microphone capture and volume through an ALSA and libasound layer owned by one audio service, and apps reach it over a socket client for playback transport and recording. The HAL object model, aggregate devices, hardware clocks and per-process audio taps have only SDK models; virtual devices and audio boxes have pure models too, but no loader or hardware path publishes them. No SDK exposes device objects.

<a id="core-audio-types"></a>
### Core Audio Types

Partial · coverage 67% · macOS 10.15 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/coreaudiotypes) · REA `ev_98c7b647aeb9a63cfda5aad9fb900d0d1f51f13a1c9a5723f27315c033167e44`

Core Audio Types is a set of C data types (buffers, channel layouts, timestamps, format descriptions, SMPTE time) shared by Core Audio. BifrOSt has no shared type set for these: the media stack passes plain rate and channel counts, interleaved S16 PCM and microseconds, and keeps its format and channel handling inside each decoder. SMPTE timecode and the OSStatus error model have no counterpart.

Gap: the speaker and file paths still build S16 streams from a rate and channel pair, and the descriptions are not verified on Midget. |

There is no multi-buffer list type shared with apps. Refreshed 2026-10-17: The shared type exists (springboard/sdk/src/audio_format.rs, AudioBufferList with to_interleaved and to_pcm16; tests audio_format::tests); the decoders and the speaker do not use it yet. |

<a id="core-media"></a>
### Core Media

OS only · coverage 75% · macOS 10.7 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/coremedia) · REA `ev_7bba1eeb711c2f0396ac0b7560393070248ba160e53405da6003b927360b0cc8`

Core Media's low-level types (sample and block buffers, CMTime, clocks and timebases, buffer queues, format descriptions) have no app-facing BifrOSt SDK equivalent. The media pipeline has internal counterparts for samples, a playback clock, frame queues, a video decoder seam and audio output, but they are owned by the media modules and the audio service rather than exposed to apps.

Apps reach playback only through the audio service and the media modules.; No rational CMTime-style time type with timescale conversion, invalid and indefinite values, or time ranges.; No timebase with rate control and timers, so apps cannot drive a timeline with a rate or time jumps.; No general block buffer or memory pool for CPU-side sample data.; No text markup model for captions and subtitles.; No per-sample attachments or sample buffer notifications..

### Core Media I/O

OS only · coverage 67% · macOS 10.7 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/coremediaio) · REA `ev_01a95278540dbb6131b1f28ed54334c81be8e4621a321f6566ff39c332adf6a1`

Core Media I/O is the API for publishing custom camera devices as system extensions (providers, devices, streams, clients, properties) and for the legacy DAL plug-in model. BifrOSt has a Linux V4L2 capture path inside the system layer that the Camera app uses, but no SDK API for apps to read cameras, and nothing that publishes a camera device to other apps.

Exact blocker: a provider publishes a camera to other apps only through a loopback capture node, and the Linux source for that is the v4l2loopback kernel module, which is not in the Arch base install, not in the repository, and not loaded by any shell service; the shell has no code that creates a /dev/video node for other apps. Writing a provider model without that node would only be a data type, so nothing was written for this row. |
| Devices (device, device source, device properties) | CMIOExtensionDevice, CMIOExtensionDeviceSource, CMIOExtensionDeviceProperties | springboard/ui/src/video_device.rs (VideoDevice | Parity | verified on Midget 0.7.25 by 7 tests. Wave 5 (w5-core-media-i-o, parity/integration 93f283b0): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. probe() enumerates /dev/video* nodes and keeps only single-planar capture devices with streaming (usable()). Discovery only; there is no device-side publishing. |
| Streams (stream, stream source, stream properties) | CMIOExtensionStream, CMIOExtensionStreamSource, CMIOExtensionStreamProperties | springboard/ui/src/video_device.rs (StreamFormat | Parity | verified on Midget 0.7.25 by 7 tests. Consumed only by the Camera app inside the shell, not exposed as a stream API. |

There is no client identity or permission check for other apps. The app sandbox in springboard/src/bare/app_policy.rs grants /dev/snd and /dev/dri but no /dev/video node. |

Not wired: BLE GATT, RTP-MIDI sockets, kernel UMP endpoints; nothing is verified on Midget yet. Note-number math in the DAW is one small use of the models.

Core Video's pixel buffers, pools, image buffer attachments, display timing and texture cache are partial app-facing models in the SDK, built on the render crate's format, pool and attachment tables. They are not wired into apps or the shell. The GPU presenter and dma-buf surfaces stay system-layer features, and Apple's IOSurface and CVReturn have no app-facing equivalent.

Gap: no app or the shell uses these buffers yet, and the presenter and media decoders do not fill them; that needs the lab machine. Built 2026-10-19: PixelBuffer::from_image, to_image (under a lock), write_image (under a read-write lock) and from_planes convert between buffers and gfx::Image for the four 32-bit RGB layouts, RGB565, NV12 and NV16 (video range, the matrix from the attachments), so a frame can go through the image filters. Decoders and the presenter still do not fill buffers. Midget check: `cargo test -p bifrost-render pixel_convert` and `cargo test -p bifrost-app pixel_buffer::tests::an_image_goes_into_a_buffer_and_comes_back_only_under_a_lock`. |

Not wired into apps or the shell, and not tested on the VM or Midget. The presenter keeps a fixed set of drawables per surface; no pool with these limits is exposed to apps |

<a id="media-intelligence"></a>
### Media Intelligence

Partial · coverage 80% · macOS 27.0 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/mediaintelligence) · REA `ev_2c9b700223e1adc5dc69aeb5346e155855b4bfa0499c492ea61bf0ef6041038c`

Media Intelligence is an on-device analysis framework for face grouping in images and highlight and keyframe selection in video. BifrOSt has no face detection, no person grouping, no highlight or keyframe analysis, and no on-device ML runtime. The only related code is the MP4 demuxer, which reads the sync-sample flags for seeking, not for analysis.

| Feature | Apple API | BifrOSt | Status | Note |

| Face grouping in images (FaceGroupAnalyzer, MediaIntelligenceImageAsset) | FaceGroupAnalyzer, MediaIntelligenceImageAsset; query faces by asset, entity or face ID | springboard/ui/src/face_group.rs | Parity | verified on Midget 0.7.25 by 6 tests. Wave 3 (w3-media-intelligence, parity/integration cf8e852d): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. No face detector and no person clustering in springboard/sdk/src or springboard/apps. The photocraft app is an upstream release (springboard/apps/photocraft-desktop/upstream.toml points at storytold/photocraft on GitHub); its source is not in this repo, so its internals cannot be checked here. |
| Best moment and highlight segments in video (VideoAnalyzer, HighlightAnalysisRequest) | VideoAnalyzer, MediaIntelligenceVideoAsset, HighlightAnalysisRequest | springboard/ui/src/highlight_rank.rs | Parity | verified on Midget 0.7.25 by 6 tests. Wave 3 (w3-media-intelligence, parity/integration cf8e852d): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. The media stack (springboard/src/media/) decodes and plays video but has no engagement or highlight scoring. filmcraft is also an upstream release (springboard/apps/filmcraft-desktop/upstream.toml), so its code is not checked here. |
| Keyframe selection for video theme (KeyFrameAnalysisRequest) | KeyFrameAnalysisRequest | springboard/ui/src/keyframe_pick.rs | Parity | verified on Midget 0.7.25 by 6 tests. Wave 3 (w3-media-intelligence, parity/integration cf8e852d): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. The demuxer exposes container sync samples for seeking, which is not the same as choosing a representative frame by content analysis. No representative-frame API exists in the SDK. |
| On-device ML analysis runtime (shared by all requests) | In-process on-device analysis, no data leaves the system (per the framework overview) | springboard/ui/src/ml_runtime.rs (AnalysisRuntime); springboard/ui/src/ml_model.rs, springboard/sdk/src/inference.rs, springboard/ui/src/tensor.rs; tests: springboard/ui/tests/parity_sdk-complete-25.rs | Partial | AnalysisRuntime loads named models once, routes every request to the model it names, refuses unknown or duplicate names and counts requests per model, tested headless in ui/tests/parity_sdk-complete-25.rs. Gap: no compute device acceleration, no model download or cache, and no shell or app client yet, which needs Midget with a deployed app. |
| Errors (MediaIntelligenceError) | MediaIntelligenceError | springboard/ui/src/media_intelligence_error.rs (MediaIntelligenceError, check_embedding, check_threshold); springboard/ui/src/face_group.rs (FaceGroups::try_insert_face, try_entities) | Partial | One typed error covers face grouping: an empty, non-finite or wrong-length embedding and a threshold outside -1 to 1 are refused with their reason, and runtime failures are carried through; tested headless in ui/tests/parity_sdk-rest-10.rs. Gap: no app-facing analysis request returns it yet, so the reference error cases for asset loading and video analysis have no counterpart. |

Gaps: Face detection and person grouping for images, with a query API by asset, entity or face ID; Video highlight scoring (engaging segments) over decoded frames; Content-based keyframe selection (representative frame) beyond container sync samples; Media analysis errors for asset loading and video analysis (face grouping errors are typed).

### Media Library

Partial · coverage 64% · macOS 10.9 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/medialibrary) · REA `ev_b2a2237afd42db6a56ffd90db72bd24caa3b0ac96dfd9819d374acb1b8ce738e`

Apple's Media Library is a read-only, deprecated Objective-C model of media sources, groups and objects (the docs point to PhotoKit and the iTunes Library framework instead). BifrOSt scans the Music and Pictures folders in two places (the Music app and the shell Photos code), but it has no app-facing SDK API for read-only media collections, and the source and group hierarchy is missing.

<a id="media-toolbox"></a>
### Media Toolbox

OS only · coverage 70% · macOS 10.9 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/mediatoolbox) · REA `ev_219054dc890874ba032143b0cbb610af3e29837791f84ca3a24b84ae33059eda`

Media Toolbox covers the audio processing tap API (MTAudioProcessingTap*), registration of professional video format readers, and localized media type names. BifrOSt has no public Media Toolbox equivalent: decoding, demuxing and playback run inside the shell's media module and are not exposed to apps, and there is no audio tap hook in audiod.

<a id="mediaextension"></a>
### MediaExtension

Partial · coverage 86% · macOS 15.0 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/mediaextension) · REA `ev_3cbae968582578d0f9a65e810ea563aa77c03cba8024aa04679f87b142212718`

MediaExtension is an extension point that lets third-party code add format readers, video decoders and RAW processors. BifrOSt has no such extension point: the video decoder seam, the demuxers and the image decoders are compiled into the desktop binary and are not pluggable by apps. The internal counterparts for format reading and video decoding exist; RAW processing does not.

| Feature | Apple API | BifrOSt | Status | Note |

| Format readers (MEFormatReader, MEFormatReaderExtension, MEByteSource) | MEFormatReader, MEFormatReaderExtension, MEFormatReaderInstantiationOptions, MEFileInfo, MEByteSource | springboard/src/media/demux/mod.rs (Pure-Rust demuxers: mp4.rs, webm.rs, mse.rs); springboard/src/media/mp4.rs | Parity | verified on Midget 0.7.25 by 17 tests. Demuxers for MP4/fMP4 and WebM are built in. No app-facing extension point, no out-of-process reader, no byte-source abstraction, no sidecar file handling. |
| Track readers and sample cursors (METrackReader, METrackInfo, MESampleCursor) | METrackReader, METrackInfo, MESampleCursor, MESampleLocation, MESampleCursorChunk, MEEstimatedSampleLocation, MEHEVCDependencyInfo | springboard/src/media/demux/mod.rs (Sample, TrackKind, CodecId, TrackInfo), springboard/core/src/mediaext.rs | Parity | verified on Midget 0.7.25 by 5 tests. Tracks and samples are parsed internally with microsecond times. No public sample cursor for seeking and stepping; the cursor API is not exposed to apps. |
| Video decoders (MEVideoDecoder, MEVideoDecoderExtension, MEDecodeFrameOptions) | MEVideoDecoder, MEVideoDecoderExtension, MEDecodeFrameOptions, MEVideoDecoderPixelBufferManager | springboard/src/media/mod.rs (VideoDecoder trait, default_decoder); springboard/src/media/hwdec/ffmpeg.rs (libavcodec via dlopen, VA-API hwaccel) | Parity | verified on Midget 0.7.25 by 7 tests. The VideoDecoder trait is an internal seam with one implementation (libavcodec, VA-API when available). Apps cannot register a decoder for a codec type. No per-frame decode options. |
| Video decoder registration by codec type (kMEVideoDecoderCodecInfoKey and related property-list keys) | kMEVideoDecoderClassImplementationIDKey, kMEVideoDecoderCodecTypeKey, kMEVideoDecoderCodecInfoKey, kMEVideoDecoderExtensionPointName | springboard/core/src/mediaext.rs | Parity | verified on Midget 0.7.25 by 7 tests. Wave 3 (w3-mediaextension, parity/integration cf8e852d): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. No property-list or manifest mechanism that declares a decoder for a four-character codec type. Codec choice is a closed enum in the desktop binary. |
| RAW processors (MERAWProcessor, MERAWProcessorExtension, MERAWProcessingParameter) | MERAWProcessor, MERAWProcessorExtension, MERAWProcessorPixelBufferManager, MERAWProcessingParameter, MERAWProcessorNotification | springboard/render/src/raw_params.rs (RawParameter, RawProcessingParameters) | Partial | Parameter ranges, clamping, reset, enable flags and key checks are tested in render/tests/parity_sdk-tests-19.rs. Gap: no RAW decoding and no processor extension point, so the parameters are not yet passed to a processor. |

Gap: extensions run in-process with no extension host, and the video decoder and RAW processor entitlements are not enforced. |
| Errors (MEError, MediaExtensionErrorDomain) | MEError, MEError.Code, MediaExtensionErrorDomain | springboard/src/media/demux/mod.rs (DemuxError), springboard/src/media/mod.rs (Error enum) | Parity | verified on Midget 0.7.25 by 8 tests. Internal error enums exist for demux and playback. They do not map to MediaExtension's error domain and codes, and no app receives them through a public error type. |

Gaps: No public extension point for third-party format readers, video decoders or RAW processors.; No public track reader or sample cursor API for apps; sample cursors are internal to springboard/src/media/demux/.; No RAW image processing (camera RAW decode, processing parameters) in springboard/render/src/imgdec.rs.; Codec manifests (a property-list dictionary with FourCC, Name and Professional) are read and registered by bifrost_ui::codec_manifest; no extension ships a decoder through one yet.; No extension host or entitlement that loads a sandboxed plug-in to read a format or decode a codec.; VideoDecoder is an internal trait with one implementation; there is no second decoder or per-frame decode options..

<a id="musickit"></a>
### MusicKit

n/a · coverage n/a · macOS 12.0 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/musickit) · REA `ev_d7690439ef1b90bf248ad8f85a289ca9bc0719af4662eccee0330454d4515528`

MusicKit is the client for Apple Music's catalog, subscriptions and tokens, which only exist as an Apple online service. BifrOSt has no catalog, subscription or Apple Music token layer, so nothing maps to it; local playback is covered by the Media Player row of the matrix instead.

| Feature | Apple API | BifrOSt | Status | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Catalog search and resource requests | MusicCatalogSearchRequest, MusicCatalogResourceRequest, Filters | nothing | n/a | Requires the Apple Music catalog API; no BifrOSt catalog service. |
| Music items (Song, Album, Artist, Playlist, Station ...) | Album, Artist, Song, Playlist, Station, Track | nothing | n/a | Catalog item model belongs to Apple Music. Local library items are a separate concern (Media Library row). |
| Authorization and subscription state | MusicAuthorization, MusicSubscription, MusicSubscriptionOffer | nothing | n/a | Apple ID and Apple Music subscription offers; BifrOSt Cloud accounts (bifrost-cloud) do not sell music. |
| Developer tokens | MusicTokenProvider, MusicDeveloperTokenProvider, automatic developer token generation | nothing | n/a | Tied to the MusicKit App Service in the Apple developer portal. |
| Music player for catalog content | ApplicationMusicPlayer, SystemMusicPlayer, MusicPlayer, PlayParameters | springboard/sdk/src/lib.rs:88 (audio service client, svc::audio) | n/a | Playback of Apple Music catalog items needs the catalog service. The audio client plays local and stream media only. |
| Artwork views | Artwork, ArtworkImage | springboard/sdk/src/widgets.rs (player artwork slot) | n/a | Artwork is supplied by the Apple Music catalog; BifrOSt apps draw their own artwork. |
| Apple Music API raw requests | MusicDataRequest, MusicDataResponse | nothing | n/a | Raw calls to the Apple Music API. Generic HTTP is in the URL session SDK (springboard/sdk/src/url.rs), but there is no Apple Music endpoint. |

Gaps: No Apple Music catalog, subscription or token service; out of scope for a Linux desktop.; Apps that expect MusicKit can use the local Media Player and radio paths instead; the matrix does not treat that as parity..

Related: [iTunes Library](#itunes-library), [Media Intents](#media-intents), [StoreKit](#storekit), [Media Library](#media-library), [ShazamKit (Media)](#shazamkit).

<a id="now-playing"></a>
### Now Playing

Partial · coverage 69% · macOS 27.0 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/nowplaying) · REA `ev_b851395bbd5ed4a24947758f6d3c4a5a2f08a78adeca6e13a0413124a2145dc8`

The shell publishes whatever the audio service plays to the lock screen Now Playing card and the Control Center media controls, with play, previous, next, seek and shuffle/repeat state. Apps have no Now Playing API: there is no local MediaSession publish, no typed content or artwork model, no feedback or playback-rate commands, and no remote-device sessions.

Gaps: No HRTF or head-tracked binaural output: the listener model gives pan gains, distance and occlusion gains only.; SDK exposes only the playback client (springboard/sdk/src/lib.rs:87); the sampler and buses live inside the DAW app and are not reusable; Occlusion is a transmission gain over boxes (sound_space Occluder); no geometry or material acoustics.; Reverb: sound_room gives reverb time and critical distance, but no applied reverb or environment effect reaches the output.; Groups and ducking: sound_group models a group gain and a ducker, but the audio service applies neither across apps..

Related: [Audio Toolbox](#audio-toolbox), [Core Audio](#core-audio), [Music Understanding](#music-understanding), [Audio Unit](#audio-unit), [AVFAudio](#avfaudio).

### PhotoKit

Partial · coverage 66% · macOS 10.11 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/photokit) · REA `ev_c5daec50d0ec7872629a366160cc42fbfa15d118ce6fd1d0e4113eb6a3df1689`

BifrOSt has a built-in Photos app that browses a folder-based library (All Photos, Favorites, Recently Deleted, Screenshots, Recents), with thumbnails, a viewer, a slideshow, a basic editor and JPEG EXIF reading. Apps get a partial PhotoKit-style API: authorization, asset fetch, thumbnails, change observation and a picker call that the shell refuses for now. There is no Live Photo, no editing extension host and no project host.

<a id="quick-look-thumbnailing"></a>
### Quick Look Thumbnailing

Partial · coverage 56% · macOS 10.15 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/quicklookthumbnailing) · REA `ev_e60d2e785c18d96337877fec2a26816888c3df03b4f9de1625c2b21080e1e058`

BifrOSt has a system thumbnails service with providers for images, text, PDF, audio and video (cover, poster frame, waveform card and a running time badge), archives, fonts and documents, a shared disk cache, an app extension point ([[preview]] with preview.render, with the system provider as the fallback), an SDK generator with tier updates and cancel, and thumbnails in Files, the Space panel and Spotlight file rows. Apple's error codes are not matched, and Desktop icons and the Dock do not show thumbnails yet.

The thumbnails service already drew PDF (first page, thumbs/pdf.rs) and video poster frames (first key frame, thumbs/media.rs poster_frame), besides text, image, audio/video cover or waveform card, font, contact, calendar, web, archive (entry count) and clipping files; unknown types get the icon. Built now: the running time badge (m:ss or h:mm:ss, bottom right) on every audio and video thumbnail (thumbs/duration.rs: duration_secs from the MP4 movie header or the audio decoder's declared length, format_duration, badge; tests in duration.rs). Live Photos and USDZ do not exist on the PC. Midget check: open Files in icon view on a folder with an .mp4, an .mp3 and a .flac: each thumbnail shows its running time in a dark pill at the bottom right; `cargo test -p springboard thumbs::duration` for the header reads. |

<a id="screen-saver"></a>
### Screen Saver

Partial · coverage 61% · macOS 10.0 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/screensaver) · REA `ev_cc2a3e312b2679aab08837530b31bc4264f252a6ac1417506af9f1d0610ddb94`

Apple's framework is a plug-in interface: a .saver bundle subclasses ScreenSaverView, which the system animates in its own engine. BifrOSt has the view lifecycle, the SS helpers, the configuration options and the idle clock as pure models in springboard/ui and springboard/core, re-exported through the SDK (springboard/sdk/src/screen_saver.rs and idle_watch.rs). It still has no .saver bundle host, no screen saver engine, and no Settings preview or configuration sheet wired to a module. The shell's idle display-off and auto-lock sit underneath, and apps do not yet receive the shell's last-input time.

<a id="accelerate"></a>
### Accelerate

Partial · coverage 68% · macOS 10.3 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/accelerate) · REA `ev_371efbd6465434fa7c238d2db92f2f8a9c41b8360f6013ec6863082d97dc6c3e`

Accelerate's vector, signal, linear algebra, sparse solver and ML APIs have no BifrOSt SDK counterpart. DEFLATE and zlib are available to apps through the SDK compression module. The system and apps contain private equivalents (quarter-turn rotation, YUV to RGBA conversion, a radix-2 FFT convolver, brightness and contrast lookup tables), but no app can call them through the SDK.

<a id="accessory-access"></a>
### Accessory Access

Partial · coverage 50% · macOS 27.0 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/accessoryaccess) · REA `ev_3028a6377a32f0776badf1386fc123695c24512c7074905b013c4690380d79f4`

Accessory Access is a USB-only framework: listeners match connected USB accessories and receive attach and detach events. BifrOSt now has the full path: the shell reads the bus, an app that declares the usb permission asks the person for one device (filters built from the same matching criteria), receives attach and detach events for devices it was granted, and opens them through the shell, which keeps the device node out of the sandbox. A hardware check on Midget remains.

| Accessory manager | AAUSBAccessoryManager (https://developer.apple.com/documentation/accessoryaccess/aausbaccessorymanager) | springboard/sdk/src/accessory_access.rs (AccessoryManager), springboard/core/src/accessory_manager.rs (AccessoryManager::sync); tests: springboard/core/tests/parity_sdk-complete-14.rs, springboard/sdk/tests/parity_sdk-complete-14.rs, springboard/src/shell/services/usb_access.rs | Partial | AccessoryManager::sync takes a full bus snapshot, detaches what is missing, attaches what is new and reports the connection ids it changed; apps reach the manager through the SDK module, and both behaviours are tested headless. Gap: no bus source feeds sync with real enumeration yet, which needs hardware and a lab check on Midget. 2026-10-19 (wave 15, usb): AccessoryManager::sync is now fed by the shell: the usb service calls usb_bus_source::poll every second, and what attached or detached becomes the events apps receive. Apps reach it through usb_access (request, devices, events), not a manager of their own. Midget check: cargo test -p springboard --features desktop-wayland usb_access::the_scan_lists_usb_and_hid_devices_but_never_protected_ones; on the device: plug and unplug a USB device and read the usb service's connected and disconnected events. |
| Accessory object | AAUSBAccessory (https://developer.apple.com/documentation/accessoryaccess/aausbaccessory) | springboard/sdk/src/accessory_access.rs (Accessory), springboard/core/src/accessory_manager.rs (Accessory), springboard/sdk/src/usb_access.rs | Partial | The device descriptors, configuration and strings are public fields, and a detached accessory keeps its identity record, tested headless in core/tests/parity_sdk-complete-14.rs. Gap: no bus source fills the strings and configuration yet, which needs hardware. 2026-10-19 (wave 15, usb): usb_access::Device carries the id, name, vendor, product, device class and interface classes of a granted accessory; open returns the configuration, interfaces and endpoints. Strings beyond the product name are not read. Midget check: cargo test -p bifrost-app usb_access:: external_accessory:: usb_printer:: (usb_access::tests::devices_and_requests_replies_decode, an_open_reply_decodes_for_usb_and_hid). |
| Matching criteria | AAUSBAccessoryMatchingCriteria (https://developer.apple.com/documentation/accessoryaccess/aausbaccessorymatchingcriteria) | springboard/sdk/src/accessory_access.rs (MatchingCriteria, DeviceMatch, InterfaceMatch), springboard/core/src/usb_descriptors.rs, springboard/sdk/src/usb_access.rs, springboard/core/src/usb_grants.rs | Partial | Criteria select by vendor, product, class, subclass and protocol, and by interface; a device with no configuration read does not match an interface criterion, tested in core/tests and sdk/tests parity_sdk-complete-14.rs. Subclass and protocol cannot be expressed in a filter; the app reads them from the open reply. Gap: the permission manifest has no USB device permission and no prompt, so an app cannot request a grant yet, which needs the sandbox and hardware. 2026-10-19 (wave 15, usb): Built: the usb and hid manifest permissions, the permission sheet (Allow Once, Always Allow, Don't Allow; Don't Allow is the default and an unanswered sheet grants nothing), grants per app and device with a cap of 32 per app, Always Allow saved in usb-app-grants.txt, Allow Once ended by app quit or unplug, a revoke switch under App Permissions, and an app asked once per run per device so it cannot nag. Midget check: cargo test -p bifrost-core usb_grants:: usb_session:: hidraw:: and cargo test -p springboard --features desktop-wayland usb_access::; Settings > Privacy & Security > App Permissions shows a USB AND HID DEVICES group (screenshot with `bifrost pc midget screen`); turn the switch off and the app's open handles close. |

<a id="app-tracking-transparency"></a>
### App Tracking Transparency

n/a · coverage n/a · macOS 11.0 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/apptrackingtransparency) · REA `ev_1811c7fce18cf52780e207134e608cf2910462b8ebfc25d4fe63a66092629add`

The framework asks the person for permission before an app tracks them across other companies' apps and websites. BifrOSt has no advertising or cross-app tracking identifier, so there is nothing to ask permission for. The permission manifest in springboard/src/bare/app_policy.rs is the nearest counterpart and covers sandbox grants, not tracking.

| Feature | Apple API | BifrOSt | Status | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Tracking authorization request | ATTrackingManager.requestTrackingAuthorization(completionHandler:) | nothing found | n/a | BifrOSt apps get no cross-app tracking identifier, so no prompt is needed. |
| Expanded interface and additional information action | requestTrackingAuthorization(preferExpandedInterface:additionalInformationAction:completionHandler:) | nothing found | n/a | Part of the same prompt; not applicable without tracking. |
| Usage description keys | NSUserTrackingUsageDescription, NSUserTrackingMarkdownUsageDescription | springboard/src/bare/app_policy.rs (permission manifest) | n/a | The manifest declares sandbox permissions such as keychain. It has no tracking key. |
| Authorization status | ATTrackingManager.trackingAuthorizationStatus, AuthorizationStatus | nothing found | n/a | No status value to report. |

### Apple Archive

Partial · coverage 50% · macOS 11.0 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/applearchive) · REA `ev_d29483e649b181c7241be638022e1dc6ebfbd3923c5a414205cc47a344dd7a4d`

BifrOSt has an app-facing archive module in the SDK: ZIP folders and single files, raw DEFLATE for buffers, strings and byte streams, a thread-count option, a custom BFEA encrypted wrapper, and (2026-10-19) the BifrOSt archive format BAR1 in bifrost_app::archive_format: attributes, directory pack and extract with path-traversal protection and size limits, Deflate, LZ4 or LZMA payloads, and signed and sealed forms. Tar reading serves app package install. The Apple Archive container byte format, its stream protocols and its encrypted archive profiles are not present.

Gaps: BAR1 is not the Apple Archive container (AAR) byte format, field keys or stream protocols; the Files app and the Archive Utility still write ZIP; File flags, access control lists and creation time are not kept in archives; extended attributes, owner, mode and times are; No Apple-compatible encrypted archive profiles and no key derivation; sealing and signing take caller-held keys; A BAR tree is held in memory per archive (bounded by Limits), entries are not streamed one at a time; Multithreaded compression covers byte streams and BAR payloads; the Files app zip writer runs as a single background job; No optimal parsing in the DEFLATE encoder, so output is larger than a full zlib encoder.

<a id="apple-cryptokit"></a>
### Apple CryptoKit

OS only · coverage 83% · macOS 10.15 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/cryptokit) · REA `ev_daa965c42360c845f78ea59d8b10278b229b5e0289fef403e27794bb99134bc7`

BifrOSt has SHA-256, HMAC-SHA256 and ChaCha20 inside the shell, used only to protect the keychain file and to verify updates and backups. Apps get no hashing, cipher, signature, key agreement or typed key API; the SDK keychain stores opaque secret bytes. Most of CryptoKit (SHA-2 384/512, SHA-3, AES-GCM, ChaCha20-Poly1305, Curve25519, NIST curves, HPKE, HKDF, post-quantum KEM and signatures, Secure Enclave) has no counterpart.

Wave 4 (w4-apple-cryptokit, parity/integration 0925691e): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. SHA-256 only, in the shell's core crate; no SDK type, no SHA-384 or SHA-512, no HashFunction protocol |
| SHA-3 hashing | SHA3_256, SHA3_384, SHA3_512 (and digest types) | springboard/core/src/sha3.rs (sha3_256 | Parity | verified on Midget 0.7.25 by 6 tests. Wave 4 (w4-apple-cryptokit, parity/integration 0925691e): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. no SHA-3 implementation in springboard/ |
| HMAC message authentication | HMAC, SymmetricKey, SymmetricKeySize | springboard/core/src/hkdf.rs (hmac_sha256) | Parity | verified on Midget 0.7.25 by 6 tests. Wave 4 (w4-apple-cryptokit, parity/integration 0925691e): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. HMAC-SHA256 is private to the keychain module; no SymmetricKey type and no HMAC API for apps |
| ChaCha20-Poly1305 (ChaChaPoly) | ChaChaPoly | springboard/core/src/chacha_poly.rs (seal, open, poly1305); springboard/sdk/src/chacha_poly.rs (ChaChaPolyKey) | Partial | RFC 8439 ChaCha20-Poly1305 with a 32-byte ChaChaPolyKey that seals to nonce, ciphertext and tag and opens only on a matching tag; tested headless against the RFC section 2.5.2 and 2.8.2 vectors in tests/parity_sdk-rest-05.rs. Gap: the keychain still uses its own HMAC-SHA256 encrypt-then-MAC (keychain.rs seal_with and open_box), and the AEAD is not verified on Midget. |

| Public-key signatures (Curve25519 Ed25519, P256, P384, P521) | Curve25519, P256, P384, P521 | springboard/ui/src/ed25519.rs | Parity | verified on Midget 0.7.25 by 12 tests. | Key agreement (X25519, SharedSecret) | Curve25519, SharedSecret | springboard/ui/src/x25519.rs | Parity | verified on Midget 0.7.25 by 7 tests. Wave 4 (theme-03, parity/integration 0925691e): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. no Diffie-Hellman or X25519 in springboard/ |

Gap: no PSK or authenticated modes, no other KEM or AEAD suites, and no SDK type for the HPKE key protocols, so apps cannot reach it yet. |
| Post-quantum KEM and signatures (ML-KEM, X-Wing, ML-DSA) | MLKEM768, MLKEM1024, XWingMLKEM768X25519, KEM, KEMPrivateKey, KEMPublicKey, MLDSA65, MLDSA87 | springboard/core/src/mlkem.rs (ML-KEM-768 and ML-KEM-1024: NTT, CBD and SampleNTT sampling, Compress, K-PKE, KeyGen/Encaps/Decaps with implicit rejection and the FIPS 203 key checks; tests mlkem::tests::*), springboard/core/src/sha3.rs (Shake: SHAKE128/256 XOF; tests shake_*), springboard/sdk/src/kem.rs (bifrost_app::kem: DecapsulationKey, EncapsulationKey, Variant; tests in kem::tests), springboard/ui/src/xwing.rs (X-Wing: SHAKE256 expansion of a 32-byte seed, ML-KEM-768 with X25519, the SHA3-256 combiner with the draft label; tests in xwing::tests), springboard/sdk/src/kem.rs (bifrost_app::kem::xwing: DecapsulationKey, EncapsulationKey; tests in kem::xwing::tests), springboard/core/src/mldsa.rs (ML-DSA-65 and ML-DSA-87: NTT, Power2Round, Decompose, hints, bit packings, SampleInBall, KeyGen/Sign/Verify with the rejection loop, pure interface with context; tests in mldsa::tests), springboard/sdk/src/signature_pq.rs (bifrost_app::signature_pq: PrivateKey, PublicKey, Variant; tests in signature_pq::tests) | Partial | ML-KEM-768 and ML-KEM-1024 are implemented from FIPS 203 with a pure model; the SDK draws the seeds from the kernel pool. ML-DSA-65 and ML-DSA-87 are implemented from FIPS 204 (sign, verify, deterministic and hedged signing, context strings); the SDK draws the signing randomness from the pool. Not checked: the official FIPS 203 and FIPS 204 known-answer vectors are not in the repo, so the tests check lengths, NTT round trips and multiplication, codecs, round trips, implicit rejection and the failure cases only; nothing is verified against other implementations, and the row is not parity until the vectors pass and it runs on Midget. X-Wing (XWingMLKEM768X25519) is implemented from draft-connolly-cfrg-xwing-kem as a 32-byte seed key, a 1216-byte encapsulation key and a 1120-byte ciphertext; the X25519 agreement refuses an all-zero result, so a small-order peer key is an error rather than an implicit-rejection secret, a choice to check against the draft. Still missing for this row: the X-Wing draft test vectors (not in the repo, so nothing is checked against other implementations), the KEM and KEMPublicKey type shapes, and the Apple-named XWingMLKEM768X25519 type. |

Gap: there are no key references, and keys are not reachable from apps outside the keychain calls; the keychain round trip needs the shell on Midget. |

Gaps: CryptoKit is in the SDK (sdk crypto_kit.rs) with SHA-2, HKDF-SHA256, AES-GCM, X25519 and Ed25519; other primitives are missing; SHA-2 is only SHA-256 and is not exposed; SHA-384, SHA-512 and SHA-3 are missing; No AES-GCM and no ChaCha20-Poly1305 with Poly1305; the shell's ChaCha20 is internal and paired with HMAC instead; No NIST curve signatures or key agreement; Ed25519 and X25519 exist; No HPKE. HKDF-SHA256 (crypto_kit.rs), ML-KEM (kem.rs) and ML-DSA (signature_pq.rs) exist; No typed key objects (SymmetricKey, key references) in the keychain API; No hardware-backed key source (Secure Enclave or TPM).

<a id="authentication-services"></a>
### Authentication Services

Partial · coverage 72% · macOS 10.15 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/authenticationservices) · REA `ev_eb4e8515f63dbb5347ffb186beb68ad982580d05bf3ac09772095c773e2d5156`

Secret storage, a web authentication session model, password generation, a credential exchange document, passkey client data and a callback route table have pure models. There is no passkey authenticator, no shared credential store or AutoFill, no Sign in with Apple, and no browser SSO broker. Most models are host-tested only and not yet wired into the shell.

<a id="cfnetwork"></a>
### CFNetwork

Partial · coverage 96% · macOS 10.8 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/cfnetwork) · REA `ev_70eacb6c8b9b4291ebcfc455d0f876fb4f8d0c9bc057f11028bf874f7e3f7c88`

The client side of HTTP is covered by URLSession in the SDK, which streams and caches responses, and by the shell's rustls HTTP/1.1 client. The Apple CFHost, CFNetService (Bonjour), proxy, diagnostics, FTP and raw stream APIs have no app-facing counterpart. Network state and DHCP are owned by the system network service, which apps cannot query through an SDK API.

URLRequest carries URL, method, body and headers. There is no raw serialized HTTP message, no response status line access and no CFHTTPMessageAppendBytes equivalent. Built 2026-10-17: raw HTTP/1.1 message model for CFHTTPMessage (build, serialize, parse, header lookup) as bifrost_app::http_message; tests http_message::tests. |

Streaming and redirects work. Persistent connections are reused, but no HTTP/2, no stream properties and no final-URL property are exposed. |

Errors are returned as Rust results with the transport message. There is no CFNetworkErrors code mapping. |

### Collaboration

n/a · coverage n/a · macOS 10.5 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/collaboration) · REA `ev_22bbc0cc89efb725e2184f62e713dedcb0c411bdb0a4a1a9a4cfe9a85d91266c`

Collaboration reads and edits identities in an identity authority (local or network directory, such as Open Directory) and shows an identity picker for access control lists. BifrOSt has one local account created by the installer and no directory service or identity authority, so there is no counterpart to cover.

| Feature | Apple API | BifrOSt | Status | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Identity authorities | CBIdentityAuthority | springboard/src/shell/account.rs (one local account) | n/a | no identity database or network directory; the installer writes one account file |
| User and group identities | CBUserIdentity, CBGroupIdentity, CBIdentity | springboard/src/bare/app_policy.rs (Account: name, uid, gid, home) | n/a | POSIX uid and gid are used for sandboxing apps, not exposed as an identity API to apps |
| Identity picker | CBIdentityPicker | none | n/a | the picker promotes records to sharing accounts; BifrOSt has no sharing-account concept |
| Access control lists | Collaboration ACL use with identities | springboard/src/bare/docbroker.rs (file grants) | n/a | file grants are per-app portal grants, not identity-based ACLs |

Gaps: No identity authority or directory lookup for users and groups (only the local account).; No identity picker sheet for choosing people to share with..

<a id="compression"></a>
### Compression

Partial · coverage 50% · macOS 10.11 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/compression) · REA `ev_cb330756976058e533cab29baea93a36094946c5054a4d4b6a5c84ce6503354e`

BifrOSt has DEFLATE and zlib encoding and decoding for apps through bifrost_app::compression, with a dynamic-Huffman encoder at three levels and an optional thread count for large inputs, and streams and filters. DEFLATE, zlib and LZ4 streams are incremental and can be flushed; LZMA streams run on finalize. It has LZ4 (block, buffer framing, and the LZ4 frame format) and LZMA (the xz container around LZMA2, with CRC32, CRC64 and SHA-256 checks) but no LZFSE or Brotli codecs, and no compression for the Files app zip writer or the PNG writer. bifrost_app::archive_format adds a BifrOSt archive container over these codecs.

| Feature | Apple API | BifrOSt | Status | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Single-step buffer compression | compression_encode_buffer, compression_encode_scratch_buffer_size | springboard/sdk/src/compression.rs (encode_buffer, encode_buffer_threaded); springboard/sdk/tests/parity_sdk-tests-20.rs | Partial | DEFLATE and zlib only; takes a Level and a thread count; returns a Vec, so no scratch buffer. Tests: parity_sdk-tests-20 zlib_header_second_byte_follows_the_level, zlib_trailer_is_the_big_endian_adler32_of_the_input, threads_change_the_bytes_but_never_the_decoded_data, every_codec_and_level_round_trips_every_sample; parity_sdk-tests-04 every_level_and_algorithm_round_trips, zlib_header_flevel_follows_the_level, zlib_trailer_is_the_adler32_of_the_input, one_thread_gives_the_same_bytes_as_the_single_step_call. Not yet verified on Midget. |
| Single-step buffer decompression | compression_decode_buffer, compression_decode_scratch_buffer_size | springboard/sdk/src/compression.rs (decode_buffer, decode_buffer_limited) over springboard/render/src/cg/pdf/inflate.rs; springboard/sdk/tests/parity_sdk-tests-20.rs | Partial | DEFLATE and zlib only; output is capped at inflate::MAX_OUT (256 MiB) or a caller-given limit. Tests: parity_sdk-tests-20 the_reference_zlib_bytes_decode_to_hello, the_decode_limit_is_inclusive_and_one_byte_less_refuses, a_deflate_stream_cut_short_is_truncated, zlib_header_with_a_method_other_than_deflate_is_invalid; parity_sdk-tests-04 zlib_reference_bytes_decode_to_hello, decode_limit_is_inclusive_and_refuses_one_byte_more, decode_reports_truncated_input. Not yet verified on Midget. |
| Algorithm selection | compression_algorithm, Algorithm (LZFSE, LZ4, LZ4_RAW, LZMA, ZLIB) | springboard/sdk/src/compression.rs (Algorithm); springboard/sdk/src/compression/lz4.rs (LZ4 block, bv41/bv4-/bv4$ buffer framing, LZ4 frame, xxHash32); springboard/sdk/src/compression/lzma.rs (xz container, LZMA2 decoder and encoder, CRC32, CRC64); springboard/sdk/tests/parity_sdk-tests-20.rs; springboard/sdk/tests/compression_lz4.rs; springboard/sdk/tests/compression_lzma.rs | Partial | LZMA is implemented as the xz container around LZMA2 (lzma.rs): a decoder for every LZMA2 chunk kind, the stream, block, index and footer checks, CRC32, CRC64 and SHA-256 checks, and an encoder with a greedy hash-chain matcher, a range encoder and a CRC64 check (lc=3, lp=0, pb=2). The level and the thread count are ignored. No xz stream made by an external tool is in the repository, so there is no external test vector: the tests cover round trips, the CRC32 and CRC64 check values, refusals and limits, and the bytes are not yet checked against another xz implementation. LZ4 is implemented (greedy block encoder, bounds-checked decoder, bv41/bv4-/bv4$ buffer framing, LZ4 frame helper with xxHash32). LZFSE, LZBITMAP and Brotli are still unsupported and fail with Unsupported. Zlib, raw Deflate, LZ4 and LZMA are wired through encode_buffer, decode_buffer_limited, Stream and the filters. Tests: parity_sdk-tests-20 zlib_raw_deflate_lz4_and_lzma_are_supported, unsupported_algorithms_are_named_in_every_buffer_and_stream_entry_point; parity_sdk-tests-04 unsupported_algorithms_fail_in_every_entry_point; compression_lz4 (host unit tests, not yet run); compression_lzma (host tests, not yet run). Not yet verified on Midget. Update 2026-10-19: LZ4 streams and filters are now incremental (see the stream row); the LZ4 and LZMA codecs themselves are unchanged. Brotli and LZFSE stay Unsupported on purpose: Brotli needs its 122 KB static dictionary, which is not in the tree, and an LZFSE codec cannot be checked here without reference vectors, so no half-compatible codec was added. Midget check: on Titan build the SDK unit-test binary with `cargo test --offline --profile fast -p bifrost-app --lib --no-run`, copy the executable it prints to Midget with `scp`, and run `ssh midget ./<that executable> compression::lz4 --test-threads 1`; every test passes. |
| Multiple-step stream compression | compression_stream, compression_stream_init, compression_stream_process, compression_stream_destroy | springboard/sdk/src/compression.rs (Stream); springboard/sdk/tests/parity_sdk-tests-20.rs; springboard/sdk/src/compression/lz4.rs (Bv4Encoder, Bv4Decoder); springboard/sdk/src/compression/dynamic.rs (Encoder::flush) | Partial | A compress stream returns each block as soon as 65535 bytes of input are in, and a decompress stream returns output as soon as each symbol completes. The decoder is a resumable state machine (compression/inflate_stream.rs) that rolls back a unit needing more input. Output does not depend on how the input is split into writes. Built 2026-10-19: Stream::flush (DEFLATE and zlib write the pending block and an empty stored block, the sync flush 00 00 ff ff; LZ4 closes its partial block) so a decoder reaches every byte written so far while the stream stays open; and LZ4 streams are now incremental (Bv4Encoder emits a bv41 or bv4- block per 64 KiB, Bv4Decoder takes any split, keeps 64 KiB of history, refuses block sizes past 16 MiB, output past the limit, unknown magic and bytes after the end marker). Still missing: LZMA streams run on finalize, and there is no flush for a decompress stream (it already returns every complete byte). Not compiled or run in this round. Built 2026-10-19: a non-ZIP archive, the BifrOSt archive (BAR1, archive_format.rs), packs a folder or one file with Deflate, LZ4 or LZMA, keeps attributes, and stays under caller Limits; its paths are relative to the packed folder. Gap: the Files app writer still uses its fixed-Huffman encoder (the encoder lives in the SDK crate, which depends on the shell crate, so the shell cannot call it without moving it), and the BAR format is not the reference byte format. Gap: ZIP extraction still reads a file only, with no stream input. Gaps: No LZFSE or Brotli codec in either direction (LZ4 block and frame and LZMA2 in an xz container are implemented); Brotli needs a static dictionary that is not in the tree, LZFSE has no reference vectors here; LZMA streams buffer their input and run on finalize; DEFLATE, zlib and LZ4 streams are incremental with a flush; DEFLATE encoder has no optimal parsing and no table sharing across blocks; output is larger than zlib at its best level; PNG writer uses a fixed-Huffman deflate (springboard/src/pngenc.rs), not the SDK dynamic encoder; Files app zip writer does not use the SDK encoder yet, so its archives are fixed-Huffman.

<a id="core-bluetooth"></a>
### Core Bluetooth

OS only · coverage 68% · macOS 10.10 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/corebluetooth) · REA `ev_3b3cd1aa3e5e44c0f56db4e34ffd432cbbc6bb126afdaf5d237767f473969fe6`

Core Bluetooth is the app-facing API for BLE central and peripheral roles, GATT services and characteristics, and advertising. BifrOSt drives the Bluetooth controller in the system layer (power, discovery over BR/EDR and LE, pairing, connect, disconnect, bonds, audio route) but exposes no SDK API to apps and has no GATT client or server code.

<a id="core-hid"></a>
### Core HID

OS only · coverage 81% · macOS 15.0 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/corehid) · REA `ev_753a243aa65ad9ea11fcc201fb9df0b957d176eca3aa12ae9d00fedf5d59ec59`

Core HID is a user-space API for discovering HID devices, reading their element values, sending reports and emulating virtual devices. BifrOSt has the kernel-side equivalent for its own shell: evdev discovery, classification of keyboards, pointers, touchscreens, power and lid devices, and a uinput keyboard for agent control. No SDK module exposes any of this to apps, and the framework's report-descriptor model is not implemented.

| Feature | Apple API | BifrOSt | Status | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Device discovery (HIDDeviceManager, DeviceMatchingCriteria) | HIDDeviceManager, HIDDeviceManager.DeviceMatchingCriteria | springboard/ui/src/hid_match.rs, springboard/sdk/src/hid_devices.rs | Parity | verified on Midget 0.7.25 by 7 tests. Wave 5 (w5-core-hid, parity/integration 93f283b0): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. Discovery runs inside the shell only. No SDK API lists devices for an app; springboard/sdk/src has no HID or device module. |
| Device classification by capability | HIDDeviceTransport, HIDDeviceLocalizationCode, usage pages (HIDUsage) | springboard/ui/src/hid_match.rs (Usage::role | Parity | verified on Midget 0.7.25 by 7 tests. Wave 5 (w5-core-hid, parity/integration 93f283b0): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. Roles covers touchscreen, pointer, touchpad, keyboard, power and lid from evdev bits. There are no HID usage pages and no transport or localization codes. |
| Report descriptor elements and collections | HIDElement, HIDElementCollection, HIDReportID, HIDReportType | springboard/ui/src/hid_report.rs | Parity | verified on Midget 0.7.25 by 7 tests. Wave 2 (theme-18, parity/integration e52c2fd0): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. BifrOSt never parses a HID report descriptor. It consumes the kernel's evdev translation. |
| Reading element values and input reports | HIDElement.Value, HIDElementUpdate, HIDDeviceClient input callbacks | springboard/src/bare/input.rs (Decoder at line 63 turns evdev records into touch and key events); springboard/ui/src/hid_report.rs (ReportDescriptor::parse, Element::value, set_value) | Partial | Report descriptors parse into fields, and field values are read and written in a payload, tested headless in springboard/ui/tests/parity_sdk-os-10.rs. Gap: the shell reads evdev events, not HID input reports, so no app receives report values. |
| Sending output reports to a device | HIDDeviceClient (set report, for example an LED) | springboard/ui/src/hid_report.rs | Parity | verified on Midget 0.7.25 by 7 tests. Nothing sets LEDs, force feedback or feature reports. |

Gap: no app can ask for a grab, and the rule is applied only in the shell's input set. |

Gap: no virtual device is created from this model, and custom report descriptors, properties and the delegate are not built. |

Gaps: No app-facing device manager: no SDK API lists HID devices, filters them by usage page or vendor, or reports hotplug to an app.; No report descriptor parsing (HIDElement, HIDElementCollection), so apps cannot read arbitrary HID devices such as custom controllers or instruments.; No output reports or feature reports (LED, force feedback, configuration) to devices.; No virtual HID device API for apps; the only virtual device is the agent uinput keyboard.; Transport and localization codes are not modelled..

Related: [HIDDriverKit](#hiddriverkit), [IOKit](#iokit), [IOUSBHost](#iousbhost), [IOBluetooth](#iobluetooth), [Game Controller](#game-controller).

<a id="core-telephony"></a>
### Core Telephony

n/a · coverage n/a · macOS 10.10 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/coretelephony) · REA `ev_2cbb4b48f94655cbf2d97e8f6c26d61c9b085b4371630c3527521cd6233caf97`

Core Telephony exposes the home cellular carrier, eSIM provisioning, subscriber information and cellular data access for iPhone and iPad hardware. BifrOSt PC has no cellular modem support and no SDK API for carrier or SIM data, so there is no counterpart to map to.

| Feature | Apple API | BifrOSt | Status | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Service information (carrier, call info) | CTTelephonyNetworkInfo; CTCarrier and CTCall (deprecated) | none | n/a | Cellular carrier data needs a modem; BifrOSt PC is a Wi-Fi and Ethernet desktop (springboard/src/net/wifi.rs) |
| eSIM provisioning | CTCellularPlanProvisioning, CTCellularPlanProvisioningRequest, CTCellularPlanProperties, CTCellularPlanCapability | none | n/a | Carrier eSIM install is Apple hardware and carrier-specific |
| SIM status and plan availability | CTCellularPlanStatus | none | n/a | No SIM hardware path in the PC build |
| Subscriber information | CTSubscriber, CTSubscriberInfo, CTSubscriberDelegate | none | n/a | Cellular subscriber identity has no PC equivalent |
| Cellular data access | CTCellularData | none | n/a | Networking on PC goes through netd (springboard/src/net/), which has no cellular path |
| Network slicing | CTSlicingManager | none | n/a | Carrier 5G feature, no counterpart |
| Errors | CTError | none | n/a | Follows from the feature rows above |

<a id="darwin-notify"></a>
### Darwin Notify

Partial · coverage 67% · macOS 10.14 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/darwinnotify) · REA `ev_525d60606f901be8b59a405caf5a5af1d6f7b2d77f2724156320402b56271398`

Darwin Notify is a system-wide, name-keyed notification facility with integer tokens, state values and kernel-level delivery. BifrOSt has no equivalent: the nearest app-facing counterpart is the Foundation-style DistributedNotificationCenter, which relays string-named broadcasts between running apps through the shell. System event names (time zone, mounts, clock, network) are not broadcast to apps by name.

The SDK sorts the user info, keeps at most 32 entries with values cut to 1024 characters, and gives the sender's own observers the same payload (distributed_user_info, tested in parity_sdk-complete-24). Headless tests: a_distributed_post_reaches_local_observers_and_is_queued_for_the_shell_sorted, a_process_local_distributed_post_sends_nothing_to_the_shell, notify_bus_calls_go_to_the_notify_bus_service_with_their_method. Only between BifrOSt apps with string names; no system-wide notification bus exists here, so posting across processes outside BifrOSt needs the lab machine. Verify on Midget for parity. |

<a id="device-management"></a>
### Device Management

n/a · coverage n/a · macOS 10.15 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/devicemanagement) · REA `ev_9cedaa1108bf8905bc8a02cfff1b7a526f03c67142bc14dbb7ad7a6e06bcb388`

Apple's MDM framework is a server-side enterprise protocol for remotely managing organization-owned Apple devices through Apple School Manager and Apple Business Manager. BifrOSt has no MDM server, enrollment, declarative management or configuration-profile support, and the Apple deployment services have no Linux counterpart.

| Feature | Apple API | BifrOSt | Status | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Device enrollment | Automated Device Enrollment, account-driven enrollment (Device enrollment topic) | nothing found | n/a | Enrollment depends on Apple School Manager or Apple Business Manager accounts |
| MDM protocol: commands, queries and check-in | Commands and queries; Check-in (MDM protocol topic) | nothing found | n/a | Apple push-token MDM channel; no equivalent in BifrOSt |
| Declarative management | Declarations; Status items (Declarative management topic) | nothing found | n/a | Apple-specific declaration and status-report format |
| Configuration profiles | Profile-specific payload keys (Configuration profiles topic) | nothing found | n/a | Apple configuration-profile payload format |
| Identity management | Platform Single Sign-on, Managed Device Attestation (Implementing device management topic) | nothing found | n/a | Apple platform identity services; BifrOSt accounts live in ~/Projects/bifrost-cloud, not in this repo |
| Deployment services | Device assignment, Roster management, App Book and Subscription Management, Apple School Manager and Apple Business APIs (Deployment services topic) | nothing found | n/a | Apple-only enterprise service APIs |

Gaps: No MDM or enterprise device-management service exists in BifrOSt; this is out of scope for a Linux desktop unless the product adds fleet management..

Related: [DeviceCheck](#devicecheck), [Authentication Services](#authentication-services), [DeviceDiscoveryExtension](#devicediscoveryextension), [Service Management](#service-management), [Managed App Distribution](#managed-app-distribution).

The dnssd C API (DNS-SD over mDNS and unicast DNS) has no BifrOSt counterpart. <a id="driverkit"></a>
### DriverKit

DriverKit is Apple's framework for user-space device drivers that ship as app extensions and are installed through System Extensions. BifrOSt has no equivalent: hardware support lives in the Linux kernel and the trusted shell, and apps get no driver API.

| Driver event management | IODispatchQueue, IOInterruptDispatchSource, IOTimerDispatchSource, IODataQueueDispatchSource, OSAction | none | n/a | kernel-side dispatch for drivers; no app-facing equivalent |
| Driver memory management | IOBufferMemoryDescriptor, IOMemoryDescriptor, IOMemoryMap | none | n/a | in-driver memory descriptors; not applicable to the Linux kernel model BifrOSt uses |
| Driver registry data types | OSArray, OSDictionary, OSData, OSNumber, OSString, OSSerialization | none | n/a | IORegistry object model; BifrOSt reads sysfs directly |
| Driver entitlements and user-client access | com.apple.developer.driverkit entitlements, IOUserClient | app sandbox (springboard/src/bare/app_policy.rs) | n/a | entitlements gate Apple driver extensions; BifrOSt's sandbox does not expose device access to apps |

Gaps: No user-space driver framework; hardware support is only in the kernel and the trusted shell; No app-facing device access API beyond the existing sandbox grants (app_policy.rs).

### Exception Handling

Partial · coverage 75% · macOS 10.0 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/exceptionhandling) · REA `ev_96f61e3a54d0509b32d7c0c45f1e80685e3801fe576b4d682ae6b97ba19abfae`

Apple's framework is one Objective-C class, NSExceptionHandler, that installs an uncaught-exception handler and lets a delegate decide per exception whether to handle and log it. BifrOSt has no app-facing exception handler API; it captures Rust panics in the system layer (panic hook writes crash.log, unclean exits are noted at the next start) and isolates panics per job in the SDK dispatch and shell job pools.

<a id="execution-policy"></a>
### Execution Policy

n/a · coverage 50% · macOS 10.15 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/executionpolicy) · REA `ev_0de80b8ab6c05378ee131c48fb040ec0a03f8539abd5fcf4a61c182a71fa8ae3`

Apple's framework lets a developer tool ask the user for an exception so that locally built software may run under the execution policy (a trust gate on code the developer built). BifrOSt has no such trust gate and no exception mechanism: every installed app launches inside a fail-closed sandbox chosen by the shell, so there is no equivalent to request or record.

| Feature | Apple API | BifrOSt | Status | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Developer tool authorization (EPDeveloperTool: authorizationStatus, requestAccess(completionHandler:)) | EPDeveloperTool | springboard/src/bare/app_policy.rs (no authorization API) | n/a | The sandbox decides what an app may touch, not whether a developer tool may be trusted. Nothing asks the user for developer-tool access, and no SDK API exposes it. |
| Execution policy exceptions (EPExecutionPolicy: addException(for:)) | EPExecutionPolicy | springboard/src/bare/app_policy.rs | n/a | The launch boundary is fail-closed with no exception path, as docs/app-isolation.md states (no unrestricted fallback). Adding an exception would weaken that design, so it is intentionally absent rather than missing. |
| Launch enforcement of app policy (the counterpart that gates which code runs) | ExecutionPolicy Constants (EPErrorDomain), EPError | springboard/sdk/src/system/execution_policy.rs (check, LaunchRefusal, DOMAIN, code, from_error); springboard/src/bare/app_policy.rs; docs/app-isolation.md | Partial | Apps can run the shell's permission check and get the refusal's domain and numeric code, with tests. The shell still makes the launch decision, and sandbox setup failures are not named yet. |
| Error reporting (EPError, EPErrorDomain) | EPError, EPErrorDomain | springboard/src/bare/app_policy.rs (PolicyError, PolicyError::of, code, domain) | Partial | PolicyError gives each policy refusal a stable domain and code, and PolicyError::of reads it back from the io::Error; tests in springboard/tests/parity_sdk-complete-46.rs. Gap: launch failures in the shell still use plain io errors, and no app receives a policy error over its socket yet. |

Gaps: No app-facing API for developer-tool access requests (EPDeveloperTool); decide with the owner whether a sideload or local-build trust prompt is wanted at all, since the current design has no exception path; Policy launch failures are not exposed to apps as a typed error domain (EPError, EPErrorDomain equivalent).

Related: [Exception Handling](#exception-handling), [Security](#security), [Endpoint Security](#endpoint-security), [Core Services](#core-services), [Security Foundation](#security-foundation).

Apple's framework connects apps to MFi hardware over Lightning, 30-pin or Bluetooth with a per-protocol byte stream. BifrOSt gives USB accessories the same shape: the shell reads the bus, the person grants one device per app, and the app gets connect and disconnect notifications, an accessory object, a session on usb.vvvv.pppp and a transport that moves the session's streams over bulk or interrupt endpoints (bifrost_app::external_accessory, usb_access). Bluetooth MFi, Lightning, MFi authentication and Wi-Fi accessory setup have no counterpart.

| Feature | Apple API | BifrOSt | Status | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|

Gap: no bus source drives attach and detach on a real device, which needs hardware and a Midget check. Refreshed 2026-10-17: the manager, registration and the notification queue are covered by sdk external_accessory.rs (AccessoryManager, register_for_notifications, take_events; tests external_accessory::tests). Only the bus source that drives attach and detach on a device remains. 2026-10-19 (wave 15, usb): The bus source now runs: the shell's usb service polls /sys/bus/usb/devices once a second into the accessory manager, and sends each app connect and disconnect events for the devices it was granted. AccessoryManager::apply_usb_event and sync_usb_devices turn those into attach and detach with the notification queue. <a id="finder-sync"></a>
### Finder Sync

Partial · coverage 88% · macOS 10.10 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/findersync) · REA `ev_f3f24717e6ac18f6d1dba32e8abd434c92851592ad666ad96d263c56c0764b88`

Finder Sync lets a third-party extension add badges, shortcut menus and toolbar buttons to the Finder and observe directories. BifrOSt has no extension point for the Files app (its Finder counterpart): apps cannot add badges, menu items or toolbar buttons to it. Directory watching and file coordination exist as SDK APIs for apps, but not as file-manager extension hooks.

<a id="force-feedback"></a>
### Force Feedback

Partial · coverage 71% · macOS 10.2 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/forcefeedback) · REA `ev_cfcdde9a3970a00d568422cade4aaff07d84740a3b46f512a0a2d9db35042d16`

Apple's Force Feedback framework is a legacy C API (FFCreateDevice, FFEffectDownload, FFEffectStart) for HID force-feedback devices such as wheels and joysticks. BifrOSt has pure models for the device capability bits, effects, device properties, haptic pulses and escape frames in springboard/core, but none is wired to an evdev node or the shell: the evdev reader does not upload effects, and the SDK's haptic() call is still dropped by the shell. Cooperative levels and polar or Cartesian directions are modelled in springboard/core/src/ff_cooperation.rs, but no input node uses them yet, and the driver plug-in interface is not exposed.

Wave 2 (theme-27, parity/integration e52c2fd0): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. evdev bitmaps are parsed for keys, abs and switches only; no check for the FF capability bit, so a wheel or gamepad with force feedback is not identified as one |
| Effect creation, download and playback | FFDeviceCreateEffect, FFEffectDownload, FFEffectStart, FFEffectStop, FFEffectUnload, FFEffectSetParameters, FFEffectGetParameters, FFEFFECT, FFPERIODIC, FFCONSTANTFORCE, FFRAMPFORCE, FFCONDITION, FFCUSTOMFORCE, FFENVELOPE | springboard/core/src/force_effect.rs | Parity | verified on Midget 0.7.25 by 16 tests. Wave 5 (theme-05, parity/integration 93f283b0): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. no EVIOCSFF upload, no FF effect structures, no EV_FF play events |
| Device properties and force-feedback state | FFDeviceGetForceFeedbackProperty, FFDeviceSetForceFeedbackProperty, FFDeviceGetForceFeedbackState, FFDeviceSendForceFeedbackCommand, FFState, FFProperty | springboard/core/src/force_effect.rs | Parity | verified on Midget 0.7.25 by 16 tests. Wave 5 (theme-05, parity/integration 93f283b0): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. no gain, autocenter or actuator-enable control |

### GSS

Partial · coverage 96% · macOS 10.14 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/gss) · REA `ev_03afbf53fe958fca77ef73ab27bde47da0f2635756db20c77c1ccb84573f0d63`

Apple's GSS framework is the GSS-API (RFC 2743/2744) for Kerberos-style authenticated sessions, message protection and name handling. BifrOSt has no GSS-API implementation, no Kerberos or krb5 code and no SDK surface for it. The only nearby work is the per-app keychain for stored passwords and Wi-Fi Enterprise (EAP) settings, which do not perform GSS security-context exchange.

Gap: no GSS library is linked, so the release calls have no C side to match. |
