<a id="hiddriverkit"></a>
### HIDDriverKit

Partial · coverage 61% · macOS 10.15 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/hiddriverkit) · REA `ev_56224fc3f71aad95df7cb680e84b7313d12904ea2c2efa90c0ef737710c346da`

BifrOSt reads human interface devices through Linux evdev in the system layer. Apps that declare the hid permission can read and write raw reports of one HID device the person picked (the shell reads /dev/hidrawN for them), parse the report descriptor into elements, and match devices by usage; keyboards, keypads and security keys are never offered. Driver authoring is n/a (the kernel owns drivers). Multitouch digitizer data and virtual HID devices for apps remain open.

| Feature | Apple API | BifrOSt | Status | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Driver authoring (HIDDriverKit C++ driver classes, system extension packaging) | HIDDriverKit, IOUserHIDEventDriver, IOUserHIDDevice, System Extensions | none; drivers are Linux kernel drivers | n/a | A user-space driver model for a desktop SDK is not planned; the Linux kernel owns HID drivers |
| Reading HID input from devices | IOHIDDevice, IOUserHIDDevice, IOHIDInterface | springboard/src/bare/input.rs:140 (Device::open, exclusive EVIOCGRAB), :178 (Device::read), springboard/core/src/hidraw.rs, springboard/src/shell/services/usb_access.rs, springboard/sdk/src/usb_access.rs | Partial | Runs in the shell; apps never open devices. Blocker: Device::open takes an exclusive grab, so an app reader would receive no events, and the shell's decoded keys and touches reach apps through the runtime input enum instead. 2026-10-19 (wave 15, usb): Apps now have an API: with the hid manifest permission and the person's consent for one device, the shell opens /dev/hidrawN (read without grabbing, so the desktop keeps the device), reads input reports on a worker and sends them as report events; output and feature reports go through hid_write, hid_get_feature and hid_set_feature. Keyboards, keypads and FIDO keys are refused outright (hidraw::protected). Midget check: cargo test -p bifrost-core usb_grants:: usb_session:: hidraw:: and cargo test -p springboard --features desktop-wayland usb_access::; on the device: plug a gamepad or a vendor HID device, grant it from an app that declares `hid`, and read Event::Report. |
| Device discovery and matching by capability | Match Criteria, kIOHIDEventServicePropertiesRequiredForMatching, IOHIDEventService | springboard/ui/src/device_match.rs, springboard/core/src/usb_grants.rs | Parity | verified on Midget 0.7.25 by 6 tests. Wave 5 (w5-hiddriverkit, parity/integration 93f283b0): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. Matching is by evdev capability, not by HID usage pairs; no app-facing matching API 2026-10-19 (wave 15, usb): Filters carry the HID usage page and usage, and the service matches them against the top-level collections read from each hidraw device's report descriptor (hidraw::top_level_usages), so an app asks for a device by usage as well as by capability. Midget check: cargo test -p bifrost-core usb_grants:: usb_session:: hidraw:: (usb_grants::tests::hid_candidates_are_always_eligible_and_filter_by_usage, hidraw::tests::top_level_usages_find_each_application_collection_once). |

Gap: no keyboard usage-pair declaration is published to the system, and keys outside the boot set (keypad, media, vendor keys) have no usage. 2026-10-19 (wave 15, usb): Raw keyboard reports are never given to apps (the hidraw path refuses keyboard collections), which is the privacy rule for HID input: an app gets keys only through the window system while it has focus. Midget check: cargo test -p bifrost-core usb_grants:: usb_session:: hidraw:: (hidraw::tests::keyboards_keypads_and_security_keys_are_protected). |
| Touch and multitouch digitizer data | IOHIDDigitizerTouchData, IOHIDDigitizerCollection | springboard/src/bare/input.rs:63-65 (protocol B decoder, first contact only), springboard/sdk/src/runtime.rs:21 (Input::Touch) | Partial | Only slot 0 is tracked; no digitizer collection or per-contact data for apps |

These mappings are tested headless in springboard/ui/tests/parity_sdk-tests-07-w7.rs. Not wired into apps or the shell and not tested on the VM or Midget. No device decoding; the eraser flag is carried on the report but to_point does not act on it. |

Synthetic input stays the shell's events service, gated by the accessibility permission; a uinput device would let an app type as the person with no consent step. Midget check: none; the events service is checked with its existing tests (services::event_services). |

Wave 2 (theme-18, parity/integration e52c2fd0): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. No API exposes HID report elements or usage tables to apps 2026-10-19 (wave 15, usb): usb_access::hid_descriptor parses the report descriptor of an opened device into bifrost_ui::hid_report elements and collections, and an element reads its field out of the payload of an Event::Report by usage. Midget check: cargo test -p bifrost-app usb_access:: external_accessory:: usb_printer:: (usb_access::tests::the_report_descriptor_of_an_opened_hid_device_parses_into_elements); on the device the same with a real device's report. |

Gaps: No app-facing API for HID elements or usage tables; raw reports are read through hidraw nodes (sdk hid_reports.rs); Stylus and pen data (pressure, tilt, eraser) is not decoded; Touch decoding tracks only the first contact (slot 0); No app-facing device matching or hotplug notification by HID usage; Synthetic input exists only for touch gestures, with no general virtual HID device API.

<a id="hypervisor"></a>
### Hypervisor

n/a · coverage 50% · macOS 10.10 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/hypervisor) · REA `ev_094daaca9b148ecb4f10e8a56d3d5ccdbb32562244264bedb754fe40a54359ab`

Apple's Hypervisor framework is a C API that lets sandboxed user-space apps create VMs and vCPUs on Apple silicon and Intel Macs. BifrOSt exposes no VM API to apps; QEMU/KVM is used only as a developer test rig for running the shell in an Arch guest, and the SDK's host module reads only the task's memory footprint from /proc.

| Feature | Apple API | BifrOSt | Status | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| VM management (hv_vm_create, hv_vm_destroy, VM configuration) | hv_vm_create(_:), hv_vm_destroy(), hv_vm_config_create(), hv_vm_config_t, hv_vm_options_t | none in springboard/sdk/src/ | n/a | Apps have no way to create a VM. A desktop SDK would not normally offer this, and apps run under the bubblewrap sandbox (springboard/src/bare/app_policy.rs). |
| vCPU management (create, run, registers) | hv_vcpu_create, hv_vcpu_run, vCPU Management collection | none | n/a | No vCPU abstraction exists in the SDK or the shell. |
| Memory mapping into guest physical address space | hv_vm_map, Memory Management collection | none | n/a | The guest-memory mapping is only the Arch VM under QEMU, not an app API. |
| Timers and time-stamp counter | hv_vcpu_get/set_vtimer_mask, hv_vcpu_get/set_vtimer_offset, hv_tsc_clock, hv_vcpu_set_tsc_relative | none | n/a | Only guest timers inside the QEMU VM are used; no SDK surface. |
| Capability queries (hv_capability, sysctl availability check) | hv_capability(_:_:), hv_capability_t | none for hypervisor capabilities; springboard/core/src/host.rs is a different thing (host CPU and memory statistics) | n/a | host.rs does not report virtualisation support, so an app could not learn whether a hypervisor is available. |
| Nested virtualisation (EL2) | hv_vm_config_get_el2_supported, hv_vm_config_set_el2_enabled | none | n/a | Apple silicon only. |
| Interrupt controllers (GIC, APIC, I/O notifiers) | GIC functions and registers, hv_vm_add_pio_notifier, hv_vcpu_apic_* functions | none | n/a | Device emulation for guests does not exist in BifrOSt. Only the QEMU test VM provides it. |
| Entitlements (com.apple.security.hypervisor, com.apple.vm.networking, com.apple.vm.device-access) | com.apple.security.hypervisor, com.apple.vm.hypervisor, com.apple.vm.networking, com.apple.vm.device-access | none | n/a | BifrOSt has no entitlement model. App isolation is in springboard/src/bare/app_policy.rs and docs/app-isolation.md. |
| Developer test rig: Arch Linux guest under QEMU/KVM | not applicable (Apple's framework is an app API) | tools/arch-vm.sh, tools/vm-install.sh, tools/vm-cycle.py, docs/arch-x86-vm.md | OS only | Developer tooling only. It runs the shell on tty1 in a KVM guest. It is not an SDK feature and no app can use it. |

Gaps: No app-facing VM API. Decision: a desktop SDK does not expose hypervisors to apps, so the Hypervisor framework is marked n/a rather than gap. Revisit only if a VM-hosting app (for example a Linux VM app) is planned.; The shell cannot report whether KVM or a hypervisor is available. host.rs covers CPU and memory statistics only..

Related: [Virtualization](#virtualization), [vmnet](#vmnet), [Paravirtualized Graphics](#paravirtualized-graphics), [Kernel](#kernel), [DriverKit](#driverkit).

<a id="inputmethodkit"></a>
### InputMethodKit

Partial · coverage 56% · macOS 10.5 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/inputmethodkit) · REA `ev_d889a7762311f1422e0f0dd0cf934d9bdcf457bd459b3adb2cd0f2726112a81b`

BifrOSt covers the client side of composition (an app text field draws marked text and reports its caret) and, since 2026-10-19, the provider side in one process: the shell loads input method folders with an Info dictionary, lists their modes in the menu bar input menu, and routes the keys of the Search field and of the focused field of an external app to the selected method, which composes through a conversion engine and offers a candidate window. Missing: a third-party provider process over the window server's input method protocol, dictionary engines (kanji, pinyin) and pointer clicks on the candidate window.

The shell scans <root>/input-methods/*/Info.plist at start. Not built: a provider that runs as its own process and connects over the window server (the shell serves no wl_seat input_method to a third party). ### IOBluetooth

Partial · coverage 66% · macOS 10.2 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/iobluetooth) · REA `ev_b3de145449eaba672251b09dc9e10a424003927602414a2428e8c63d785e6b7c`

The shell drives the radio (power, discovery, Just Works pairing, connect, disconnect, forget) and routes audio to a connected headset through the kernel mgmt socket. No app-facing Bluetooth SDK exists, and none of the RFCOMM, OBEX, SDP, hands-free or user-notification classes have a counterpart.

Gaps: Apps list devices and read a pending pairing code through the SDK (bluetooth_service.rs), but pairing itself lives only in the Settings Bluetooth page (springboard/src/shell/pages.rs).; No reusable device selector sheet or panel (IOBluetoothDeviceSelectorController).; No passkey or numeric comparison pairing: pairing is hardwired to NoInputNoOutput (springboard/src/bare/bluetooth.rs:68-69), so devices that need a PIN or passkey cannot pair.; No live SDP query: springboard/core/src/bt_service_browser.rs filters a service list it is given (UUID allow list, cancel); the radio service discovery is not implemented.; No Bluetooth object push or file transfer (IOBluetoothObjectPushUIController). springboard/src/net/share.rs covers LAN sharing only.; No UUID filter for pairing (addAllowedUUID and clearAllowedUUIDs).; The Apple reference types (BluetoothKeyboardReturnType, the IOBluetoothUI constants and functions) have no BifrOSt counterpart..

Related: [IOBluetooth](#iobluetooth), [Core Bluetooth](#core-bluetooth), [Application Services](#application-services), [CoreAudioKit](#coreaudiokit), [IOKit](#iokit).

<a id="iokit"></a>
### IOKit

OS only · coverage 71% · macOS 10.0 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/iokit) · REA `ev_3eeb0b1b38dd6644082af26946ee505e9c85f8208ce87b029dbec5cfd26293fa`

IOKit's device-access layer exists on BifrOSt only in the Linux system layer (sysfs, /dev nodes, DRM, evdev, v4l2, ALSA control, Bluetooth), used by the shell and daemons. Apps get no device-registry, matching, notification or driver-call API, so the framework is not offered to SDK apps; the serial-port modem sample has no counterpart.

Wave 5 (w5-iokit, parity/integration 93f283b0): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. <a id="iosurface"></a>
### IOSurface

OS only · coverage 77% · macOS 10.6 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/iosurface) · REA `ev_42009e926440152a976795c45dfa85700886eb1922c23e8ee5c3daa24fd77a86`

The system layer shares buffers across processes with memfd and fd passing, and imports GPU dma-bufs with format and modifier metadata. Apps get no IOSurface-like SDK type: they receive shared memory only as internal pixel copies, with no lookup by ID, attributes, purgeability or colour space.

<a id="iousbhost"></a>
### IOUSBHost

Partial · coverage 50% · macOS 10.15 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/iousbhost) · REA `ev_a8792b7a789634fc2e35b8dfc894673ef8d9fe7860fc71b9c0e72e944432958c`

IOUSBHost lets apps talk to custom USB devices. BifrOSt gives an app that declares the usb permission raw access to one device the person picked on a permission sheet: the shell opens the usbfs node, applies claim, endpoint and control rules (usb_session) and runs the transfers on a worker, and apps get descriptors, bulk, interrupt and control I/O and attach events through bifrost_app::usb_access. System-driven classes (audio, HID, storage, video, hubs, smart cards) are never offered. Isochronous streaming and a hardware check on Midget remain.

| Feature | Apple API | BifrOSt | Status | Note |

| Device driver access (claim, configure, descriptors, device requests) | IOUSBHostDevice, IOUSBHostObject | springboard/sdk/src/usb_device.rs (plan_claim, ClaimPlan), springboard/core/src/usb_claim.rs, springboard/core/src/usb_descriptors.rs, springboard/src/shell/services/usb_access.rs, springboard/sdk/src/usb_access.rs, springboard/core/src/usb_session.rs | Partial | An app can plan a claim (configuration and alternate-setting requests in order, and the pipes the interface opens), and the setup packets and descriptors are encoded and parsed in the inline tests of usb_claim.rs and usb_descriptors.rs. Gap: nothing sends the requests and the sandbox binds no /dev/bus/usb, which needs hardware and a Midget check. Refreshed 2026-10-17: covered by springboard/core/src/usb_claim.rs; tests usb_claim::tests. 2026-10-19 (wave 15, usb): Built the path an app takes: the usb manifest permission, a permission sheet where the person picks one device (Allow Once, Always Allow, Don't Allow), and the shell's usb service, which opens /dev/bus/usb/BBB/DDD itself, reads the descriptors and runs claim, release, alternate setting, reset and control requests through usb_session::Session on a worker thread. No device node enters the sandbox. Interfaces of classes the system drives cannot be claimed. Remaining: needs a device check on Midget. Midget check: cargo test -p bifrost-core usb_grants:: usb_session:: hidraw:: and cargo test -p springboard --features desktop-wayland usb_access::; on the device: plug a USB serial adapter (vendor-specific interface) into Midget, run an app that declares `usb` in its manifest and calls usb_access::request from the front window, then usb_access::open and claim(0); the Done events carry the result. Settings > Privacy & Security > App Permissions shows a USB AND HID DEVICES group (screenshot with `bifrost pc midget screen`). |

No pipe or stream abstraction exposed to apps. The triage note says likely n/a; the framework's stated use cases (cameras, audio, scanners, printers, MIDI, hubs) are mostly covered at the system layer, which leaves custom device drivers as the real gap..

<a id="kernel"></a>
### Kernel

n/a · coverage 50% · macOS 10.0 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/kernel) · REA `ev_04dec99a6c1f7907fcfd7ec40e64ed5108319340a7176281b72ffd17f6eb1c2a`

Kernel covers kernel extensions (kexts), the IOKit base classes for in-kernel drivers, and BSD/Mach kernel interfaces. These are specific to Apple's XNU kernel and kext loading model. BifrOSt runs on Linux, where drivers are in-tree or loaded by the Linux kernel itself, and BifrOSt ships no kernel extension or kernel-resident API for apps.

| Feature | Apple API | BifrOSt | Status | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Kernel extensions (kexts) | Implementing drivers, system extensions, and kexts; Installing a Custom Kernel Extension | nothing found | n/a | Apple kext loading does not exist on Linux; BifrOSt has no kext installer |
| Kernel debugging | Debugging a Custom Kernel Extension; Generating a Non-Maskable Interrupt | nothing found | n/a | Two-Mac kernel debugging is an Apple workflow; no counterpart in BifrOSt |
| IOKit driver base classes | IOKit Fundamentals, Hardware Families, Driver Support, IOService, IOCatalogue | springboard/sdk/src/device_registry.rs (devices, Matching, changes, DeviceWatch); springboard/src/bare/kms.rs (DRM card probing), springboard/src/media/v4l2.rs | Partial | Apps list the devices of a class with their sysfs properties, match them and see arrivals and removals by polling, with tests. There is no driver model, and drivers stay in the system. |
| BSD and Mach interfaces | kern, sys, vfs, vm, net, mach, mach-o | Linux kernel via libc calls (for example springboard/src/bare/bluetooth.rs uses AF_BLUETOOTH sockets) | n/a | Apple's XNU interfaces are not a public surface on Linux; apps use the Linux kernel through libc |
| Kernel-side event services | IOEventLink, IOWorkGroup, IOServiceStateNotificationDispatchSource | nothing found | n/a | Specific to IOKit's kernel service registry |
| Deprecated kernel symbols | Deprecated Symbols | n/a | n/a | Nothing to map; BifrOSt has no equivalent of Apple's deprecation list |

Gaps: No SDK API for app code to talk to a driver or read device state from the kernel; hardware access sits in the shell and daemons (springboard/src/bare/).; No kernel-level debugging workflow comparable to Apple's kext debugging (not needed for an app SDK, recorded for completeness)..

Apple's framework tests the signed identity of code on disk and of running or launching processes. BifrOSt has no code-signing or signature verification, so none of the requirement DSL has a counterpart. The launch path only starts installed packages under the shell-assigned app ID inside a sandbox, and update downloads are checked against a SHA-256 hash that is not signed.

<a id="nearby-interaction"></a>
### Nearby Interaction

n/a · coverage n/a · macOS 11.0 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/nearbyinteraction) · REA `ev_1828ebad5c74125853aabafac5b4e0392f187f5e74db9d6803dc95c97170a409`

Nearby Interaction measures the distance and direction of peers with the Ultra Wideband chip in iPhone, Apple Watch and partnered accessories. BifrOSt has no UWB hardware support and no ranging API, and the desktop targets PC hardware that has no UWB chip, so the framework has no counterpart.

| Feature | Apple API | BifrOSt | Status | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Session and peer discovery | NISession, NISessionDelegate, discovery tokens | none | n/a | Needs a UWB chip on both peers; PC hardware has none. |
| Peer configuration (iPhone and Watch) | NINearbyPeerConfiguration | none | n/a | Distance and direction from UWB; Apple-only hardware. |
| Third-party accessory configuration | NINearbyAccessoryConfiguration, Nearby Interaction Accessory Protocol | none | n/a | Accessory ranging needs a UWB radio on the host. |
| Nearby object measurements | NINearbyObject (distance, direction) | none | n/a | No ranging data source on this platform. |
| Session convergence and user coaching | NIAlgorithmConvergence, camera assistance | none | n/a | Depends on the UWB and ARKit session pipeline. |
| Downlink time difference of arrival ranging | DL-TDOA anchor ranging (articles) | none | n/a | Anchor-based indoor positioning needs UWB anchors. |
| Errors | NIError, NIErrorDomain | none | n/a | Error domain only exists with the framework. |

<a id="open-directory"></a>
### Open Directory

Partial · coverage 75% · macOS 10.6 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/opendirectory) · REA `ev_eb014de815128860cdce7126c81b1af84b12a2dbedf415d0b3a6a5b4a663a05f`

Open Directory authenticates users and searches records (people, groups) in directory nodes such as LDAP servers. BifrOSt has one local account created by the installer, no directory node, no record query API and no directory authentication, so the directory client API is a gap. The contacts app and cloud sync are separate services and are not a directory counterpart.

<a id="security-foundation"></a>
### Security Foundation

OS only · coverage 80% · macOS 10.3 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/securityfoundation) · REA `ev_f75e957e9582ab8459e2254a01008807bc72d24ac30eac7da69739d0d1063421`

The framework has one class, SFAuthorization, which asks the system to authorize and preauthorize named rights for privileged operations. BifrOSt enforces per-app manifest permissions in the shell and has no SDK call for an app to check or request an authorization right; the nearest app-facing feature is the permission-gated keychain.

The System framework is a set of typed Swift wrappers over POSIX file calls (FileDescriptor, FilePath, Stat, FileMode, Errno). BifrOSt has the same POSIX operations at the Linux and Rust level, plus file grants that hand apps a descriptor, advisory directory locks and a filesystem watch, but no SDK wrapper types for any of them.

<a id="system-configuration"></a>
### System Configuration

Partial · coverage 81% · macOS 10.1 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/systemconfiguration) · REA `ev_3c473dc73369865634e53ae372d69276d20d90ddf9fc920cd2ad08b375c39189`

<a id="system-extensions"></a>
### System Extensions

n/a · coverage n/a · macOS 10.15 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/systemextensions) · REA `ev_2fb525b4803b2144c8acdd8d49445eee0a4283b3e2c13f424f2524c500ec9d77`

Apple's user-space driver and system extension install and activation flow (OSSystemExtensionManager) is tied to macOS kernel policy and the notarized app bundle. BifrOSt has no equivalent install-and-approve path for user-space drivers; hardware drivers live in the Linux kernel and the shell talks to them directly.

| Feature | Apple API | BifrOSt | Status | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Extension activation and deactivation | OSSystemExtensionManager, OSSystemExtensionRequest | none | n/a | Linux kernel modules are loaded by the system, not by apps; no user approval prompt exists |
| Usage descriptions | NSSystemExtensionUsageDescriptionKey, OSBundleUsageDescriptionKey | none | n/a | no install prompt for drivers |
| Extension info and workspace observer | OSSystemExtensionInfo, OSSystemExtensionsWorkspace | none | n/a | no user-space extension registry |
| Errors | OSSystemExtensionError | none | n/a |  |
| Entitlements | System Extension Entitlement, System Extension Redistributable Entitlement | app_policy.rs sandbox profile (no extension entitlement) | n/a | app sandbox is bubblewrap, not Apple entitlements |

<a id="vmnet"></a>
### vmnet

n/a · coverage n/a · macOS 10.10 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/vmnet) · REA `ev_fc8cb262a7ba99feed2a25b9e670f9e003f8e735ab46dfcca3b83721660e17d2`

vmnet is Apple's virtual NIC API for guest operating systems on macOS, with host and shared (NAT) modes and an entitlement gate. BifrOSt has no virtual machine framework or app-facing virtual network API; only a QEMU test harness for its own Arch VM.

| Feature | Apple API | BifrOSt | Status | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Network configuration (host and shared modes) | vmnet_network_configuration_create, vmnet_network_create | none | n/a | no app-facing virtual network object |
| Starting and stopping virtual interfaces | vmnet_start_interface, vmnet_interface_start_with_network, vmnet_stop_interface | none | n/a | tools/arch-vm.sh starts a QEMU guest, not an SDK call |
| Interface events | vmnet_interface_set_event_callback, interface_event_t | none | n/a | no event API for guest interfaces |
| Reading and writing packets | vmnet_read, vmnet_write, vmpktdesc | none | n/a | host packet I/O lives in springboard/src/net/mod.rs, not exposed to apps |
| DHCP reservations and port forwarding | vmnet_network_configuration_add_dhcp_reservation, vmnet_network_configuration_add_port_forwarding_rule | none | n/a | no DHCP server for guests in BifrOSt |
| Entitlement for virtual networking | com.apple.vm.networking | none | n/a | app isolation is springboard/src/bare/app_policy.rs (bubblewrap); no networking entitlement |

Gaps: No virtual machine framework for apps (no guest NIC, host or NAT mode API).; No app-facing packet I/O or interface events; springboard/src/net/mod.rs is private to the shell..

Related: [Hypervisor](#hypervisor), [Virtualization](#virtualization), [System Configuration](#system-configuration), [Network](#network), [ThreadNetwork](#thread-network).

<a id="xpc"></a>
### XPC

Partial · coverage 75% · macOS 10.10 · [official docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/xpc) · REA `ev_6d848fe5109f2f68624bff910f3992869ede9c354b0893f935a14563d9eaf856`

BifrOSt has no XPC API for apps: no XPCSession, XPCListener, XPC activities or XPC event handlers. It covers part of the same job with a service supervisor (bifrostd, restarts services with backoff), a root daemon contract (privd), an owner-only JSON-RPC control socket per app, in-process and distributed notifications, and ProcessInfo activities that keep an app running in the background.

| Feature | Apple API | BifrOSt | Status | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Creating XPC services (XPCListener, XPCSession, XPCReceivedMessage) | XPCListener, XPCSession, XPCReceivedMessage, xpc_listener_t, xpc_session_t | springboard/sdk/src/peer_session.rs | Parity | verified on Midget 0.7.25 by 9 tests. Wave 3 (theme-21, parity/integration cf8e852d): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. No SDK type for typed peer-to-peer sessions with a listener. The control socket is one request per connection and is served by the app for agents and tools, not for app-to-app messaging. The shell-to-app protocol is internal and not exposed to apps. |
| XPC services launched on demand, shut down when idle, restarted on crash | XPC services (managed by launchd) | springboard/sdk/src/service_client.rs (ServiceClient::connect, ping, call; ServiceId; socket_path); springboard/bifrostd/src/lib.rs (socket activation on the first connection, restart with backoff, new version swapped in after a ping); springboard/sdk/src/service_management.rs (SMAppService, mainApp only) | Partial | An app connects to a service socket and the supervisor starts the service on that first connection; the client's connect, ping, call, timeout and disconnect paths are tested headless in sdk/tests/parity_sdk-rest-14.rs. Gap: services are never shut down when idle, an app cannot declare a service in its manifest, and the lab machine has not confirmed that a sandboxed app reaches a live service. |
| Privileged helper and root daemon | XPC services with privileged LaunchDaemon (via Service Management) | docs/privd-protocol.md (contract for the root daemon bifrost-privd, proto 1); springboard/src/bin/portal.rs (D-Bus org.freedesktop.portal.Settings service) | OS only | The blocker is access, not the protocol: bifrost-privd accepts a connection only from the shell, bifrost-mcp or a root tool (checked by the peer executable path), and the app sandbox never binds its socket, so no app can call it. The portal is a D-Bus service for Linux toolkit apps, not an XPC counterpart. |
| XPC activities (background activity scheduling) | XPC activities (xpc_activity_register, criteria, defer and check-in) | springboard/sdk/src/process_info.rs (ActivityOptions: USER_INITIATED, LATENCY_CRITICAL, BACKGROUND, IDLE_SYSTEM_SLEEP_DISABLED); springboard/sdk/src/runtime.rs:213 (beginActivity keeps an app running after it leaves the foreground); springboard/sdk/src/activity_schedule.rs (ActivityCriteria, ActivitySchedule, run_if_due); tests: springboard/sdk/tests/parity_sdk-complete-38.rs | Partial | Activity criteria with an interval, a tolerance and repeats, and a schedule that decides wait, run or finished and runs work when due, are tested headless. Gap: the scheduler is an in-process model driven by the caller's clock, so the system does not run it, and the shell's throttling hints are not tied to it; the lab machine must verify the system behaviour. |
| XPC events (on-demand IOKit and notification events) | XPC events (IOKit matching, system notifications delivered to a service) | springboard/sdk/src/notification.rs (NotificationCenter, DistributedNotificationCenter add_observer, post, post_with); tests: springboard/sdk/tests/parity_sdk-tests-01b.rs; springboard/sdk/src/workspace.rs (NSWorkspace-style calls) | Partial | Named notifications work inside the app process, with a distributed variant that posts through the shell. Nothing wakes a service from a device or IOKit event. Headless tests (headless_notification_center_* in sdk/tests) cover observer filtering, removal, the distributed namespace, and that post_with asks the shell to relay the post while the sender's observers hear it. Delivery to other running apps depends on the shell and was not verified on Midget. |
| XPC objects (typed values for messages) | XPC objects (xpc_dictionary_t, xpc_array_t, xpc_string_t and others) | springboard/sdk/src/coding.rs (Codable and plist); bifrost_core::json (JSON values used by control and intent calls) | Parity | verified on Midget 0.7.25 by 11 tests. Messages are JSON or plist, not XPC objects. Apps that already use Codable or JSON can exchange data, but there is no typed XPC object model or XPC-compatible wire format. |
| XPC connections and endpoints (XPCEndpoint, anonymous listeners) | XPCEndpoint, XPCPeerRequirement, xpc_endpoint_t | springboard/sdk/src/peer_session.rs | Parity | verified on Midget 0.7.25 by 9 tests. Wave 3 (theme-21, parity/integration cf8e852d): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. No endpoint objects that can be passed between processes, and no peer requirement or code-signing check. Access control is owner-UID only. |
| Peer validation (XPCPeerRequirement) | XPCPeerRequirement, xpc_peer_requirement_t | springboard/sdk/src/control.rs (SO_PEERCRED owner check); springboard/src/bare/app_policy.rs (bubblewrap sandbox policy for apps) | Parity | verified on Midget 0.7.25 by 8 tests. The owner UID check covers same-user access. There is no requirement on bundle identity, signing or entitlements, because BifrOSt has no code-signing peer check. |

Gaps: No SDK API for XPC-style typed sessions between an app and a helper (XPCListener, XPCSession, XPCReceivedMessage).; No app-facing way to declare a helper service that the system launches on demand and shuts down when idle. bifrostd only restarts services.; No XPC activity scheduler (criteria, intervals, deferral, system-run callback) in the SDK.; No endpoint objects for passing a connection to another process, and no peer requirement beyond the owner UID.; No event wake-up for services from device or IOKit events..
